title: SEED Solar PV Installation Training 2026: Free Solar Energy Training in Lagos and Abeokuta with COREN Certification
summary: The Siemens Energy Education and Development (SEED) Solar PV Installation (SPVI) Training is offering professionals and technicians an opportunity to strengthen their technical knowledge and practical skills in solar photovoltaic installation and renewable energy technologies. The training is supported by the Nigerian Energy Support Programme (NESP), a technical assistance programme co-funded by the European Union and the German Government and implemented by GIZ. Designed to respond to the growing demand for technically competent renewable energy professionals, the programme combines classroom-based theoretical instruction with practical, hands-on learning, technical site visits and competency assessments. Successful participants will also receive COREN Certification upon completion of the training. Importantly, the training itself is offered free of charge , and the cost of certification is also covered. Meals will be provided on training days, although participants will be responsible for their own accommodation and transportation. The particular training stream covered by the application form will be conducted in Lagos State and Abeokuta, Ogun State , with participants required to attend the training in person for three weeks in September 2026. About the SEED Solar PV Installation Training The SEED Solar PV Installation Training is focused on developing practical and technical capacity in the renewable energy sector, particularly for individuals who are working or intending to work in solar photovoltaic installation and related areas. Solar photovoltaic technology is increasingly important in the transition towards cleaner and more accessible energy. As demand for solar energy systems continues to grow, there is a corresponding need for technicians and professionals who possess the technical competencies required to install, operate and work with solar PV systems safely and effectively. The training therefore provides an opportunity for participants to develop competencies that can support their professional development and participation in Nigeria s renewable energy industry. Rather than being limited exclusively to applicants with conventional academic qualifications, the programme specifically encourages applications from individuals coming through both formal educational pathways and practical or experience-based pathways . This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to people who have gained technical knowledge through education as well as those whose skills have been developed through hands-on work and practical experience. Who Is Organising and Supporting the Training? The training is associated with the Siemens Energy Education and Development (SEED) initiative and is supported by the Nigerian Energy Support Programme (NESP) . NESP is described in the application information as a technical assistance programme that is: Co-funded by the European Union . Co-funded by the German Government . Implemented by GIZ . Through this support, the programme is designed to contribute to technical capacity development in Nigeria s renewable energy sector. The involvement of these institutions also makes the training relevant to broader efforts to improve technical skills and strengthen the renewable energy workforce. What Does the Solar PV Installation Training Cover? The programme is structured around several complementary forms of learning. Participants will not only receive theoretical information but will also have opportunities to apply their knowledge in practical settings. The training will combine: 1. Theoretical Instruction Participants will receive theoretical instruction designed to build their understanding of solar PV installation and related technical concepts. The theoretical component provides an important foundation for practical work because solar PV installation requires technicians to understand how systems function, how different components interact and how installations should be approached from a technical and safety perspective. 2. Hands-On Practical Training A major component of the programme is practical training. Participants will have the opportunity to develop their technical competencies through hands-on activities rather than relying solely on classroom instruction. This practical focus can be particularly valuable for people preparing to enter the renewable energy sector or professionals seeking to strengthen existing technical skills. 3. Technical Site Visits The programme will also include technical site visits. Site visits can provide participants with exposure to practical applications of renewable energy technologies and help connect theoretical concepts with real-world installations and working environments. This component is particularly useful for participants who want to understand how solar PV systems and technical processes are applied beyond a classroom setting. 4. Competency Assessments The training will include competency assessments to evaluate participants knowledge and practical capabilities. Assessment is an important part of technical training because it provides an opportunity to demonstrate that the competencies developed during the programme can be applied effectively. 5. COREN Certification Participants who successfully complete the training will receive COREN Certification , according to the application information. The certification component adds an important professional dimension to the programme and may be valuable to individuals seeking to strengthen their professional credentials in the technical and engineering-related space. Training Locations For this particular stream, training will take place at two locations: Lagos State Abeokuta, Ogun State Applicants are required to indicate their preferred training location when completing the application form. The form provides the following location choices: Abeokuta, Ogun State Lagos State Applicants should therefore consider their ability to attend their selected location before submitting the application. Three-Week In-Person Training Requirement One of the most important requirements stated in the application form is the ability to attend the programme in person for three weeks during September 2026 . The application specifically asks candidates whether they are able to attend the training physically for three weeks. This means that the opportunity is not presented as an online training programme. Applicants should be prepared to participate physically at one of the designated training locations. Before applying, prospective participants should therefore consider: Their availability throughout the three-week training period. Their ability to travel to and from the selected training location. Their ability to arrange accommodation if they live outside the training location. Their ability to cover transportation costs. Their ability to attend the required training activities in person. Is the SEED Solar PV Installation Training Free? Yes. The training is stated to be free of charge . The programme information specifically indicates that: The training is free . The cost of certification is free . Meals will be provided on training days . This significantly reduces the direct cost of participating in the programme and makes the opportunity accessible to individuals who may otherwise find professional technical training financially difficult to pursue. However, applicants should carefully note that not every participation-related expense is covered. What Costs Are Not Covered? While the training and certification are free, GIZ-NESP and Siemens Energy will not provide accommodation or transportation support during the training. Participants should therefore make their own arrangements for these costs. This means that applicants travelling from another city or location may need to budget for: Transportation to and from the training location. Local transportation where necessary. Accommodation for the duration of the training, if required. Any other personal expenses not specifically identified as covered by the programme. The provision of meals on training days can help reduce daily expenses, but participants should still make adequate arrangements for other costs associated with attending a three-week in-person programme. Who Is Encouraged to Apply? The training is designed primarily for individuals interested in developing or strengthening their technical and practical competencies in the renewable energy sector. The application information specifically describes the target audience as: Professionals working in the renewable energy sector . Technicians working in the renewable energy sector . Professionals seeking to work in the renewable energy sector . Technicians seeking to work in the renewable energy sector . Individuals coming through formal educational backgrounds . Individuals coming through practical or experience-based pathways . The inclusion of both formal and experience-based pathways is an important feature of the programme. Applicants should therefore not assume that only people with traditional academic qualifications can apply. The information explicitly encourages candidates with practical or experience-based backgrounds to submit applications. Formal and Experience-Based Applicants One of the notable aspects of this opportunity is its recognition of different routes through which people develop technical competencies. Applicants with Formal Education Individuals who have acquired relevant knowledge through formal education may find the programme useful for strengthening their technical and practical capabilities. Academic or technical education can provide theoretical foundations, while practical training can help participants apply that knowledge in real-world settings. Applicants with Practical Experience The programme also welcomes applicants who have developed their knowledge and abilities through practical experience. This is significant for technicians and other individuals who may have gained skills through hands-on work rather than exclusively through formal academic programmes. The application information therefore takes a broader approach to technical capacity development by recognising both educational and practical pathways. What Are the Requirements for Applicants? Based on the information provided in the application form, prospective participants should meet the following key conditions: Have an interest in working in the renewable energy sector, or already be working in the sector. Be a professional or technician seeking to develop relevant competencies. Be willing to participate in the technical and practical components of the programme. Be able to attend the training in person for three weeks in September 2026 . Select either Lagos State or Abeokuta, Ogun State as the preferred training location. Be prepared to arrange their own accommodation and transportation. Be able to commit to the programme s training requirements. The application form also requests basic personal and contact information, including the applicant s full name, gender, phone number and email address. Information Required on the Application Form Applicants should be prepared to provide several details when completing the application. The form requests: Full Name Applicants are asked to provide their surname and first name. Gender The available options shown in the form are: Female Male Phone Number Applicants must provide a telephone contact. Email Address A valid email address is required for the application. Preferred Training Location Applicants can select: Abeokuta, Ogun State Lagos State Availability for In-Person Training Applicants must confirm whether they can attend the training in person for three weeks from September 2026. The form identifies the questions as required, meaning applicants should ensure that the requested information is completed before submitting the application. Important Google Account and Privacy Notice The application is presented through Google Forms. The form indicates that the name, email address and photo associated with the applicant s Google Account will be recorded when the applicant uploads files and submits the form . Applicants should therefore review the information associated with the Google Account they use when accessing the application and ensure that they are comfortable with the information being recorded as part of the submission process. Why This Training Opportunity Is Valuable The SEED Solar PV Installation Training provides several potential benefits for people interested in renewable energy and technical careers. Free Technical Training The programme removes the tuition cost associated with the training. Participants do not have to pay for the training itself. Free Certification The cost of certification is also covered, meaning participants can complete the programme without paying the stated certification costs. Practical Skills Development The hands-on nature of the training can help participants develop practical competencies relevant to solar PV installation. Exposure to Real-World Applications Technical site visits can provide participants with exposure to practical applications and professional environments within the renewable energy field. Competency Assessment Participants will have their competencies assessed as part of the training, providing a structured way of evaluating the knowledge and skills developed during the programme. COREN Certification Successful completion comes with COREN Certification, according to the information provided in the application form. Meals During Training Days Meals will be provided on training days, helping to reduce some of the daily expenses associated with attending the programme. Opportunity for Different Educational Backgrounds The programme encourages applications from both formally educated candidates and individuals whose competencies have been developed through practical experience. Things Applicants Should Consider Before Applying Although the training is free, prospective applicants should carefully consider the logistical requirements. The programme is in person , and participants must attend for three weeks. This makes availability one of the most important considerations before submitting an application. Applicants should also remember that accommodation and transportation are not provided. Someone living outside Lagos or Abeokuta, for example, should determine whether they can realistically travel to the training location and remain there for the duration of the programme. A strong applicant should therefore: Confirm availability for the full three-week period. Select a training location they can reasonably access. Plan transportation in advance. Arrange accommodation independently if necessary. Ensure their phone number and email address are accurate. Review all required application questions before submission. Use an appropriate Google Account when completing the form. Submit the application with accurate personal information. Deadline for the SEED Solar PV Installation Training Application Deadline: Not specified in the application information provided. The supplied application form states that the training will take place for three weeks from September 2026 , but it does not provide a specific application closing date. Applicants should therefore verify the application page for any updated closing date or submission instructions before applying. Since the training is scheduled for September 2026, prospective applicants should avoid waiting until the last moment to complete the form. APPLY HERE How to Apply for the SEED Solar PV Installation Training Interested applicants should complete the official SEED Solar PV Installation Training application form and provide the required personal and contact information. The application requires candidates to select their preferred location between Abeokuta, Ogun State and Lagos State and confirm that they can attend the training physically for three weeks in September 2026. Applicants should ensure that all required sections are completed accurately before submitting the form. Visit HERE to learn more about the SEED Solar PV Installation Training 2026. Conclusion The SEED Solar PV Installation Training presents an important opportunity for professionals and technicians who want to strengthen their technical competencies and pursue opportunities in Nigeria s growing renewable energy sector. Supported through the Nigerian Energy Support Programme and implemented by GIZ, with Siemens Energy involved through the SEED initiative, the programme combines theoretical learning, hands-on practical training, technical site visits and competency assessments. One of the strongest features of the opportunity is that the training and certification are free , while meals are provided on training days. Participants should, however, be prepared to cover their own accommodation and transportation expenses. The programme is also notable for welcoming candidates from both formal educational and practical, experience-based backgrounds. This broad approach gives technicians and aspiring renewable energy professionals with different educational pathways an opportunity to develop relevant skills. Applicants should pay particular attention to the three-week, in-person attendance requirement in Lagos or Abeokuta, Ogun State , and should confirm that they can commit to the programme before applying. Since no specific application deadline is provided in the supplied information, prospective applicants should check the official application form for the latest submission information. title: JET Programme 2027: Apply to Teach English in Japan for at Least One Year as an Assistant Language Teacher
summary: The Government of Japan is inviting applications from young South Africans interested in gaining international teaching and cultural exchange experience through the Japan Exchange and Teaching (JET) Programme 2027 . The programme offers successful participants an opportunity to spend at least one year in Japan working as Assistant Language Teachers (ALTs) while contributing to internationalisation, foreign-language education, and people-to-people exchange at the local level. Administered through a collaboration involving Japanese government ministries and agencies, the JET Programme is one of the world’s largest international exchange programmes. It brings university graduates from participating countries to Japan to work with local governments, schools, boards of education, and other organisations. For South African graduates with an interest in education, language, Japanese culture, international relations, community engagement, and cross-cultural communication, the JET Programme provides an opportunity to live and work in Japan while developing professional and intercultural skills. JET Programme 2027 Overview The Japan Exchange and Teaching (JET) Programme was established to promote grassroots internationalisation in Japan. Participants work with local communities and educational institutions, helping strengthen understanding between Japan and other countries. For the 2027 intake, the Embassy of Japan in South Africa is calling for applications from young South Africans who would like to spend at least one year in Japan as Assistant Language Teachers. Key details Programme: Japan Exchange and Teaching (JET) Programme 2027 Position: Assistant Language Teacher (ALT) Host country: Japan Recruiting country: South Africa Duration: Generally one year Target applicants: Young South African university graduates Work environment: Elementary, junior high and senior high schools, local boards of education and related institutions Application method: Courier with a tracking number or hand delivery Application deadline: 4:00 PM, 16 October 2026 Application location: Embassy of Japan, 259 Baines Street, Groenkloof, Pretoria, 0181 Selection notification: Successful and unsuccessful applicants will be contacted by email What Is the JET Programme? The JET Programme is an international exchange initiative administered through cooperation among several Japanese institutions, including the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) , Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) , Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) , and the Council of Local Authorities for International Relations (CLAIR) . Its primary objective is to promote grassroots internationalisation at the local level. Rather than focusing only on international exchange at the national or diplomatic level, the programme places participants directly within Japanese communities. Participants interact with students, teachers, local government employees and community members, allowing cultural exchange to take place through everyday professional and community activities. The programme also seeks to create long-term international networks. Participants are expected to contribute positively to mutual understanding between Japan and their home countries while gaining a deeper understanding of Japanese society and culture. JET Programme History and Global Reach The JET Programme has developed considerably since its establishment in 1987. According to the Embassy of Japan in South Africa, the programme began with participants from only four countries. Over the years, it has expanded to include participants from 54 countries , with 5,993 participants as of 2025 . Across the history of the programme, more than 80,000 people from 82 countries have participated. This extensive international participation demonstrates the scale of the JET Programme and its emphasis on creating connections between Japan and communities around the world. The programme has also developed a strong reputation both within Japan and internationally. Participants are regarded as representatives of their respective countries and are therefore expected to conduct themselves responsibly and contribute constructively to international understanding. Assistant Language Teacher Position The 2027 opportunity highlighted by the Embassy of Japan in South Africa is for applicants interested in serving as Assistant Language Teachers (ALTs) . ALTs are primarily placed in educational settings, including: Local boards of education Elementary schools Junior high schools Senior high schools Participants work under the guidance of language-teacher consultants, Japanese teachers of foreign languages, school principals, boards of education, or other designated supervisors. The precise working environment and responsibilities can vary depending on the Contracting Organisation to which an individual is assigned. Duties and Responsibilities of an ALT The role is broader than simply standing in front of a classroom and teaching English. Participants can become involved in different educational and cultural activities depending on the needs of their school or Contracting Organisation. Typical responsibilities may include the following. 1. Assisting with foreign-language classes ALTs assist Japanese teachers with foreign-language lessons in elementary, junior high and senior high schools. This can involve supporting classroom activities, language practice, communication exercises and other activities designed to help students develop their foreign-language abilities. The exact nature of classroom involvement may depend on the school, teaching arrangements and instructions provided by the relevant supervisor. 2. Supporting foreign-language activities in elementary schools Participants may also assist with foreign-language activities for younger learners. This gives ALTs an opportunity to introduce language learning in engaging and accessible ways while interacting directly with Japanese pupils. 3. Helping prepare teaching materials ALTs may contribute to the preparation of materials used for foreign-language education. This could involve helping teachers develop language-learning resources or providing information and examples that support classroom instruction. 4. Supporting language training for teachers Participants may assist with language training for Japanese teachers of foreign languages or other language-related activities. Their perspective as international participants can be useful in providing practical language knowledge and insights into how English and other foreign languages are used. 5. Participating in extracurricular and club activities The JET Programme can extend beyond formal classroom instruction. ALTs may cooperate with extracurricular activities and school clubs, allowing them to interact with students in less formal educational environments. 6. Providing language-related information Participants may provide information to teachers and language consultants on matters such as: Word usage Pronunciation Language expressions Other language-related subjects This responsibility allows participants to contribute their knowledge of their own language and culture to the Japanese education system. 7. Supporting foreign-language speech contests ALTs may also assist with foreign-language speech contests. This could include helping students prepare, providing language-related guidance or supporting the organisation of such activities, depending on the requirements of the school or Contracting Organisation. 8. Supporting local international exchange activities One of the most important elements of the JET Programme is international exchange. Participants may cooperate in local international exchange activities, helping communities develop greater awareness and understanding of other countries and cultures. 9. Performing other duties as required Participants may be assigned additional duties considered necessary by their supervisor or school principal. Because assignments differ between Contracting Organisations, applicants should understand that the precise responsibilities of an ALT can vary. Where Do JET Participants Work? JET participants are generally appointed by Japanese prefectures, municipalities, private schools and other Contracting Organisations. This means that successful applicants are not necessarily assigned to one specific city or region in Japan. Their eventual placement depends on the organisation to which they are appointed. Participants can therefore expect their experience to be shaped partly by their assigned community, school and local working environment. For someone interested in experiencing Japanese life beyond major tourist destinations, this aspect of the programme can be particularly significant because placements can connect participants with local communities and educational institutions. One-Year Participation Period Participants are generally appointed for a one-year period . The programme is therefore designed as a substantial international experience rather than a short-term visit. Successful applicants should be prepared to live and work in Japan for the duration of their appointment. The Embassy of Japan also emphasises that participants should avoid withdrawing from the programme after receiving an assignment or ending their participation early, as doing so can create significant difficulties for the Contracting Organisation and affect the administration of the programme. Applicants should therefore consider the commitment carefully before applying. Financial Support and Transportation According to the Embassy of Japan s information, the cost of transportation from the participant s place of origin to Japan, as well as remuneration, is funded by Japanese taxpayers through the Contracting Organisation where the participant is appointed. This means successful participants receive financial support connected to their participation and employment under the programme. Because participants serve as staff members of their respective Contracting Organisations, they are expected to observe applicable rules and behave responsibly. The financial arrangements therefore form part of a broader employment and public-service structure rather than being simply a study-abroad scholarship. Professional and Personal Development Opportunities The JET Programme can provide participants with an opportunity to develop skills that extend beyond language education. Living and working in another country can expose participants to new professional environments, educational systems and cultural practices. Participants can potentially develop experience in areas such as: Classroom support and education Public speaking and communication Cross-cultural communication Community engagement International relations Cultural exchange Teamwork Adaptability Interpersonal communication Working in a foreign professional environment Understanding Japanese society and culture For graduates interested in careers involving international development, education, communications, diplomacy, international organisations, cultural exchange or global affairs, such experience can provide useful exposure. Expectations of JET Participants JET participants are regarded as representatives of their respective countries. The Embassy of Japan therefore stresses the importance of responsible behaviour and mutual understanding. Applicants should understand that the programme is not solely about travelling to Japan. Participants are expected to make a meaningful contribution to the communities in which they live and work. The Embassy indicates that desirable participants should be: Adaptable Mentally capable of performing their duties Physically capable of performing their duties Deeply interested in Japan Responsible in their activities Committed to promoting mutual understanding between nations Participants should therefore be prepared to adapt to a different cultural and professional environment. Why the International Exchange Element Matters International exchange is central to the JET Programme. An ALT from South Africa, for example, does more than assist with language education. Their presence can give Japanese students and community members opportunities to learn about South Africa and interact with someone from a different cultural background. At the same time, the participant gains first-hand exposure to Japanese culture and society. This two-way exchange is one of the fundamental purposes of the programme. Participants are encouraged to build relationships with the communities where they are placed, contributing to a broader international network that can continue beyond their period in Japan. Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity is particularly relevant to young South African university graduates who are interested in combining professional experience with international cultural exchange. Potentially suitable applicants may include graduates interested in: Teaching and education English-language education International exchange Japanese culture International development Global communication Community engagement Cross-cultural relations International careers Applicants should also be comfortable with the responsibilities associated with representing their country in an international programme. Application Deadline for JET Programme 2027 The deadline is 4:00 PM on 16 October 2026 . Importantly, applications must arrive at the Embassy of Japan by the deadline . Applicants should therefore not wait until the final day to send their documents. The Embassy specifically instructs applicants to either courier their complete application package with a tracking number or hand deliver it to the designated address. Application address Embassy of Japan JET Programme 259 Baines Street Groenkloof Pretoria 0181 South Africa Applicants using courier services should allow sufficient time for the package to arrive before the stated deadline. How to Apply for the JET Programme 2027 Applicants should carefully review the official JET Programme information and application documentation before preparing their submissions. The basic submission process indicated by the Embassy is: Review the official JET Programme information and application requirements. Complete the required application documentation. Prepare the complete application package. Check that all required documents have been included. Submit the package by courier with a tracking number or hand deliver it to the Embassy of Japan in Pretoria. Ensure that the application arrives by 4:00 PM on 16 October 2026 . Wait for notification by email regarding the outcome of the application. Applicants should ensure that their submissions are complete and comply with the instructions in the official application documentation. Selection Results The Embassy of Japan states that both successful and unsuccessful applicants will be contacted by email. Applicants are specifically requested not to contact the Embassy to enquire about the outcome of their application . It is therefore important for applicants to monitor the email address provided in their application after submission. To APPLY download the application form HERE . Important Considerations Before Applying The JET Programme can be a major international and professional opportunity, but applicants should understand the commitment involved. Before applying, prospective participants should consider whether they are prepared to: Live in Japan for at least one year. Adapt to a different cultural and social environment. Work within the Japanese education system. Follow the instructions of their supervisors and Contracting Organisations. Interact professionally with students, teachers and community members. Represent South Africa responsibly. Participate actively in international and cultural exchange. Accept the responsibilities associated with their assigned position. Commit to the programme rather than treating it simply as an opportunity for travel. The programme is intended for individuals who can make a meaningful contribution while adapting to life and work in Japan. Visit HERE to learn more about the JET Programme 2027. Conclusion The JET Programme 2027 offers young South African university graduates an opportunity to spend at least one year in Japan while working as Assistant Language Teachers and contributing to international exchange. The programme combines language education, professional experience, community engagement and cultural exchange. Participants can work alongside Japanese teachers and educational authorities, support foreign-language classes, assist with teaching materials and extracurricular activities, contribute to speech contests and participate in local international exchange initiatives. Beyond the professional responsibilities, the programme provides an opportunity to experience Japanese society from within a local community while helping Japanese students and residents learn more about South Africa and the wider world. Interested South African graduates should begin preparing their applications well before the deadline. The complete application package must arrive at the Embassy of Japan in Pretoria no later than 4:00 PM on 16 October 2026 . For the official application instructions, detailed information and application forms, applicants should consult the Embassy of Japan in South Africa s official JET Programme information before submitting their documents. title: Fully Funded PhD Positions in AI for Agriculture at New Mexico State University, USA – Spring or Fall 2027
summary: The Niu Lab at New Mexico State University (NMSU) is inviting applications from highly motivated prospective PhD students interested in advancing the use of artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, computer vision and related technologies in agriculture. The fully funded PhD positions provide an opportunity for students to undertake interdisciplinary research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and agricultural applications, with an anticipated start in Spring or Fall 2027 . The opportunity is particularly suitable for graduates in computer science, engineering, agricultural engineering and closely related disciplines who want to pursue advanced research focused on developing intelligent technologies for productive and sustainable agriculture. According to the opportunity announcement, the Niu Lab is recruiting multiple PhD students to join NMSU s Department of Computer Science and work across artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, robotics and agriculture. Overview of the PhD Opportunity The positions are hosted by the Niu Lab at New Mexico State University and will be supervised by Dr. Haoyu Niu . The selected PhD students will conduct research in an interdisciplinary environment, working with several NMSU units and agricultural research partners. The research brings together computer science and agricultural applications, creating opportunities for students to work on technologies capable of addressing real-world challenges in modern agriculture. The anticipated programme start is Spring or Fall 2027 , depending on the position and successful applicant. What Makes These PhD Positions Fully Funded? One of the major advantages of the opportunity is that each position comes with several forms of financial and academic support. Successful PhD students will receive: A stipend to support their graduate studies and living expenses. Tuition coverage , helping reduce the financial burden associated with pursuing a doctoral degree. Health insurance as part of the funding package. Conference travel support , providing opportunities for students to participate in academic and research conferences and share their work with the wider scientific community. The attached announcement specifically states that each position includes a stipend, tuition coverage, health insurance and conference travel support. This combination makes the opportunity particularly attractive to students seeking a funded doctoral research pathway in artificial intelligence, robotics, computer vision and agricultural technology. Research Areas Covered by the PhD Positions The PhD positions focus on several closely connected areas of artificial intelligence and agricultural technology. Applicants are expected to have an academic background or strong research interest in at least one of the listed areas. 1. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Students may conduct research involving: Artificial intelligence Machine learning Deep learning Reinforcement learning These areas can be applied to agricultural problems requiring intelligent prediction, analysis, automation and decision-making. Applicants with previous research experience in AI or machine learning are therefore well positioned to demonstrate their suitability for the positions. 2. Computer Vision and Multimodal Sensing Another major research area is computer vision and multimodal sensing . This area is relevant to agricultural systems that need to collect and interpret visual or other forms of sensor information. Students interested in using cameras, sensors and AI-based analysis to understand agricultural environments may find this research direction particularly relevant. 3. Robotics and Autonomous Systems The positions also cover robotics and autonomous systems , including: Unmanned aerial vehicles Unmanned ground vehicles Autonomous navigation Robotic agricultural applications This research area provides opportunities to explore how intelligent machines can operate in agricultural environments with reduced human intervention. 4. Digital Twins and Agricultural Simulation Another research direction is digital twins and simulation for agricultural systems . Students working in this area may explore computational representations and simulations of agricultural systems as tools for research, analysis and decision-making. The announcement identifies AI and machine learning, computer vision and multimodal sensing, robotics and autonomous systems, and digital twins and simulation for agricultural systems as key areas of research interest. Interdisciplinary Research Environment The PhD students will not work exclusively within one academic discipline. Under the supervision of Dr. Haoyu Niu, students will collaborate with: NMSU s Institute for Applied Practice in AI and Machine Learning (IAAM) The College of Agricultural, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences The NMSU Agricultural Experiment Station Researchers and collaborators working across artificial intelligence and agriculture This interdisciplinary structure is important because the research is designed to connect advanced computational technologies with practical agricultural challenges. Students will therefore have the opportunity to work at the intersection of technical research and agricultural applications rather than studying artificial intelligence in isolation. Qualifications and Eligibility Requirements Applicants should have an appropriate academic background and demonstrate an interest in research relevant to the positions. Academic Qualifications Applicants should hold a: B.S. degree , or M.S. degree in one of the following areas: Computer Science Computer Engineering Electrical Engineering Electronic Engineering Mechanical Engineering Agricultural Engineering A closely related field The announcement specifically requires a B.S. or M.S. degree in one of these disciplines or a closely related area. Research Background or Interest Applicants should have an academic background or strong research interest in one or more of the following: Artificial intelligence Machine learning Deep learning Reinforcement learning Computer vision Multimodal sensing Robotics Autonomous systems Unmanned aerial vehicles Unmanned ground vehicles Digital twins Agricultural systems simulation Having relevant research experience can help demonstrate an applicant s preparedness for doctoral-level research. Programming Skills Proficiency in C++ or Python is required for the positions. Experience with ROS or ROS 2 is described as desirable. This means applicants with programming experience in Python or C++, particularly those who have applied these skills to artificial intelligence, robotics, computer vision, machine learning or related research projects, may be well suited to the opportunity. Applicants with experience using ROS or ROS 2 can also demonstrate additional preparation for research involving robotics and autonomous systems. Willingness to Conduct Field Experiments The PhD positions are not limited to laboratory or computer-based research. Applicants must be willing to conduct field experiments . This requirement is particularly relevant because the research is connected to agriculture and may involve testing AI-enabled systems, sensing technologies, autonomous platforms or other technologies in real agricultural environments. Prospective students should therefore be comfortable with an interdisciplinary research approach that may combine: Computational research; Programming and AI development; Data collection and analysis; Robotics or sensing technologies; and Agricultural field experiments. Communication and Teamwork Skills Applicants should also possess: Strong written communication skills; Strong oral communication skills; and The ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary research team. These skills are important for PhD researchers because doctoral research often involves collaboration with researchers from different academic backgrounds, presentation of findings, preparation of research publications and communication of technical results. About the Principal Investigator The positions are supervised by Dr. Haoyu Niu , who earned his Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from the University of California, Merced, in 2022 . His research is focused on the intersection of: Artificial intelligence; Computer vision; Autonomous robotics; and Precision agriculture. According to the announcement, his research has a particular focus on AI-enabled robotic systems for crop monitoring . His work integrates: Vision-based sensing; Autonomous navigation; Sensor fusion; and Intelligent decision-making. The overall objective is to develop practical technologies that can contribute to productive and sustainable agriculture . This research profile makes the PhD positions particularly relevant to applicants who want to pursue careers in AI-enabled agriculture, agricultural robotics, precision agriculture, autonomous systems, computer vision or intelligent sensing. How to Apply for the Fully Funded PhD Positions Interested applicants are required to submit their application materials directly by email to Dr. Haoyu Niu. Applicants should prepare the following: 1. Curriculum Vitae Submit an updated CV highlighting relevant: Academic qualifications; Research experience; Programming skills; Publications; Projects; Technical skills; and Other experience relevant to AI, robotics, computer vision, machine learning or agriculture. 2. Academic Transcripts Applicants should provide their academic transcripts as part of the application. These should demonstrate their academic preparation for doctoral-level research. 3. Samples of Relevant Work Applicants should also provide samples demonstrating their previous research or technical work. Examples specifically mentioned in the announcement include: Publications; Project reports; and A portfolio. Applicants should therefore select work that demonstrates their capabilities and research interests in areas relevant to the PhD positions. The application materials should be emailed to Dr. Haoyu Niu at hniu@nmsu.edu . Required Email Subject Line Applicants should use the following format as the email subject: “Your Name_PhD Application” Using the requested subject line can help ensure that the application is clearly identified and processed appropriately. title: Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship 2027: Prestigious African Leadership Fellowship for Emerging Leaders Across Africa
summary: The Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship Programme 2027 is inviting nominations for the next generation of high-potential African leaders who are expected to take on significant leadership roles and contribute to Africa s transformation over the coming years. Organised by the African Leadership Institute (AFLI) , the Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship is the organisation s flagship leadership development programme. The programme has been offered since 2006 and is designed to identify, develop and connect promising young African leaders across different sectors of society. For the Class of 2027 , approximately 25 high-potential individuals from across Africa will ultimately be selected through a rigorous and competitive process. However, unlike many fellowship programmes, individuals cannot directly apply or nominate themselves . Candidates must first be nominated by another person and, following the nomination and screening stages, eligible nominees will be invited to complete the full fellowship application. The programme is designed for Africans between 30 and 39 years of age who demonstrate strong leadership potential and the capacity to contribute meaningfully to Africa s social, economic and political transformation. Nomination deadline for the Class of 2027: September 20, 2026, at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time. The subsequent candidate application process is scheduled to begin around September 25, 2026 , with applications and letters of recommendation due by October 25, 2026, at midnight Johannesburg time . About the African Leadership Institute The African Leadership Institute (AFLI) is focused on nurturing and strengthening leadership capabilities across Africa, particularly among young people who demonstrate exceptional leadership potential. The Institute s broader objective is to develop a network of high-potential African leaders who can progress into senior leadership positions within their respective fields over the following five to ten years. AFLI seeks to develop leaders who will not only advance professionally but also remain actively engaged in creating positive change across Africa. The Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship is the Institute s flagship programme through which it pursues this objective. The fellowship has been running since 2006 , creating a network of alumni who have participated in leadership learning and development activities designed to strengthen their experiences, insights, leadership tools and confidence. What Is the Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship? The Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship Programme is a prestigious leadership development programme aimed at identifying and developing the next generation of African leaders. Each year, approximately 25 high-potential individuals from across Africa are selected following a rigorous competitive selection process. The programme targets individuals who are expected to become influential leaders in their respective fields over the next five to ten years. Importantly, the fellowship is not limited to one profession or sector. The programme is intended for emerging leaders across all sectors of African society , meaning that candidates can come from different professional, social, economic, public, private, civil society and other leadership backgrounds. The central question is not simply what sector an individual works in, but whether the person demonstrates the leadership potential, experience and commitment necessary to contribute to Africa s transformation. The Purpose of the Tutu Fellowship The fellowship is designed around the idea that Africa s future depends significantly on the development of capable, ethical and transformative leaders. AFLI therefore seeks individuals who have already demonstrated leadership potential and who can develop into influential leaders in their respective fields. Through the fellowship, selected participants receive leadership learning activities intended to strengthen: Leadership experience Strategic insight Personal confidence Leadership tools Understanding of complex African challenges Capacity to influence positive change Professional networks Collaboration across sectors and countries The programme also seeks to create a lasting network of fellows who can support one another and contribute to Africa s transformation beyond the fellowship itself. Approximately 25 Fellows Will Be Selected The Archbishop Tutu Fellowship is highly selective. For each annual class, approximately 25 individuals are selected from across Africa. This means that becoming a Tutu Fellow is a competitive achievement. The programme describes its selected participants as some of the continent s most promising future leaders and specifically targets individuals expected to rise into top leadership positions within their areas of activity over the next five to ten years. Applicants and nominators should therefore understand that meeting the basic age and geographic requirements does not automatically result in selection. The selection process is designed to identify candidates who demonstrate exceptional leadership potential and a strong capacity to contribute to the transformation of Africa. Who Is the Fellowship Designed For? The programme is designed for high-potential African leaders between 30 and 39 years of age . The fellowship is not restricted to one professional discipline. Potential candidates may come from sectors such as: Government and public service Business and entrepreneurship Civil society Non-governmental organisations Education Academia and research Media and communications Technology Finance Development Health Law Agriculture Arts and culture Social enterprise Community development International development Other sectors of society The key consideration is the candidate s leadership potential and capacity to contribute to positive change. Age Requirement for the Class of 2027 Candidates must be between: 30 and 39 years of age. The nomination form explicitly requires the nominator to confirm the candidate s age. Applicants outside the specified age range should not be nominated for the programme. Prospective candidates should therefore verify their age eligibility before approaching a potential nominator. An Important Difference: You Cannot Apply Directly One of the most important aspects of the Archbishop Tutu Fellowship is that direct applications are not accepted . Individuals interested in becoming Tutu Fellows must first be nominated by another person . This means: You cannot nominate yourself. You cannot submit a direct application without first being nominated. You need someone else to put your name forward. Only one nomination is necessary. Multiple nominations may be regarded as abuse of the nomination process. The programme specifically advises interested individuals who wish to be considered to read the relevant candidate guidance and seek nomination. How the Nomination Process Works The nomination process is designed to identify individuals who have demonstrated strong leadership potential. A nominator must provide information about both themselves and the candidate. The nomination form asks the nominator to provide: Their name Email address Position or job title How long they have known the candidate The capacity in which they know the candidate Confirmation that they have contacted the candidate Confirmation that the candidate has given permission to be nominated The nominator must therefore have some meaningful knowledge of the candidate. The form provides different options for how long the nominator has known the candidate, including: 1 year 2 years 2+ years 5+ years 10+ years The form also asks the nominator to explain the capacity in which they know the candidate. Click HERE to fill the nomination form. Candidate Information Required During Nomination The nomination form requires several details about the proposed candidate. These include: Candidate s first name Candidate s last name Age Gender Nationality Country of residence Occupation Candidate s personal email address Relevant information concerning inhibiting factors The nominator s motivation for recommending the candidate The candidate must therefore give the nominator permission to submit the nomination. Candidate Permission Is Required The nomination form specifically asks: Has the nominator contacted the candidate and obtained permission to nominate them? The available responses are: Yes No This means individuals should not be nominated without their knowledge and permission. Anyone considering nominating a colleague, professional contact, community leader or other person should first discuss the opportunity with that individual. The Importance of the Nominator s Motivation One of the most significant parts of the nomination form is the section requiring the nominator to explain why the candidate would be a strong fit for the fellowship. The programme specifically asks nominators to provide personal insight into the candidate rather than simply copying the person s CV or biography. The nominator is encouraged to address questions such as: What makes this candidate a special and successful leader? Why does the candidate stand out from other potential leaders? What evidence demonstrates the candidate s leadership ability? How could the candidate s leadership contribute to Africa s transformation? How could the candidate s leadership contribute to improving the lives of people across the continent? This section is limited to 2,700 characters . Do Not Simply Copy the Candidate s CV The nomination guidance makes an important distinction between listing achievements and explaining why the person is an exceptional leadership candidate. Nominators are specifically advised not to copy and paste the candidate s CV or biography. Instead, the nominator should provide personal insight that selectors would not obtain simply by reading a résumé. This means the strongest nominations should explain the candidate s leadership character, influence, achievements and potential in a compelling and personal way. For example, a nominator could explain how they have observed the candidate: Lead a difficult initiative Mobilise communities Solve complex problems Influence institutional change Build effective teams Create employment or economic opportunities Improve public services Develop innovative solutions Advocate for marginalised communities Drive social or environmental change Demonstrate ethical leadership The objective is to help selectors understand the person behind the résumé. Nationality and African Eligibility The nomination form provides a comprehensive list of African countries and includes an option for candidates who were born outside Africa . The African countries listed include: Algeria Angola Benin Botswana Burkina Faso Burundi Cabo Verde Cameroon Central African Republic Chad Comoros Democratic Republic of the Congo Republic of the Congo Côte d Ivoire Djibouti Egypt Equatorial Guinea Eritrea Eswatini Ethiopia Gabon Gambia Ghana Guinea Guinea-Bissau Kenya Lesotho Liberia Libya Madagascar Malawi Mali Mauritania Mauritius Morocco Mozambique Namibia Niger Nigeria Rwanda São Tomé and Príncipe Senegal Seychelles Sierra Leone Somalia South Africa South Sudan Sudan Tanzania Togo Tunisia Uganda Zambia Zimbabwe The form s inclusion of Born out of Africa is important for candidates whose circumstances require clarification concerning their place of birth and African nationality. Prospective candidates should provide accurate nationality and residence information when being nominated. Gender Eligibility The nomination form provides the following gender options: Male Female Non-binary The inclusion of these options demonstrates that the nomination process is not presented as being limited to one gender. The Selection Process for the Class of 2027 The Class of 2027 selection process follows several stages. According to the updated AFLI schedule provided for the 2027 cycle, the process is structured approximately as follows. Stage 1: Invited Nominations Open August 26, 2026 Invited nominations for the Class of 2027 begin on August 26, 2026. This marks the opening of the nomination stage through which prospective candidates can be put forward for consideration. Stage 2: Nominations Close September 20, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time This is the critical deadline for nominations. The nomination deadline is described as a hard deadline . The nomination form will be taken down at the deadline and nominations submitted afterward will not be accepted. Stage 3: Screening of Nominees Following the nomination deadline, AFLI will screen the submitted nominees. The screening process is expected to take approximately: One week to 10 days after nominations close , depending on the number of nominations received. Stage 4: Candidate Application Begins The candidate application process is expected to begin: On or around September 25, 2026. Candidates who progress through the nomination and screening stage will then be able to proceed with the formal fellowship application. Stage 5: Candidate Application Deadline The deadline for the full fellowship application is: October 25, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time. This is separate from the September 20 nomination deadline. Prospective candidates and their nominators should therefore understand that there are two important deadlines : September 20, 2026: nomination deadline October 25, 2026: candidate application deadline Stage 6: Recommendation Letter Deadline Letters of recommendation from referees are also due by: October 25, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time. Candidates should therefore begin preparing their referees well in advance. Stage 7: Selection Process Begins The formal selection process is scheduled to begin in: Early November 2026. Stage 8: Shortlisted Candidates Informed Shortlisted candidates are expected to be informed around: Mid-December 2026. Stage 9: Final Selection The selectors are expected to finalise the Class of 2027 by: Mid-January 2027. Stage 10: Final Candidate Communication Invitation emails are expected to be sent to Associates and Reserves beginning in: February 2027. Stage 11: Status of Applications All candidates are expected to receive a status notification as the selection process progresses. Most candidates are expected to receive status communications around November or December 2026, while finalists will receive status communication in early 2027. Stage 12: Announcement of the Class of 2027 The Class of 2027 will be announced before the first programme workshop in South Africa. The information provided does not give an exact announcement date. The Nomination Deadline Is a Hard Deadline A particularly important warning from AFLI concerns the nomination deadline. The programme explicitly describes the deadline as a hard deadline . This means candidates and nominators should not wait until the final hours to submit the nomination. Technical problems can prevent a form from being successfully submitted. The nomination guidance specifically warns against assuming that a last-minute submission will be successful. Nominators are therefore encouraged to submit their nominations well before the deadline. Why Early Submission Matters Online application systems can experience problems for many reasons, including: Slow internet connections Browser problems Server congestion Incorrect information Form errors Difficulty uploading information Connectivity interruptions Because the nomination deadline is hard, a technical problem occurring shortly before midnight does not necessarily result in an extension. The programme therefore advises nominators to submit early. The Role of Referees For candidates who progress to the formal application stage, letters of recommendation are an important component of the selection process. The deadline for recommendation letters for the Class of 2027 is: October 25, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg time. Candidates should therefore identify appropriate referees early and make sure they understand the deadline. A candidate should ideally select people who can provide meaningful evidence of their leadership, professional achievements, character and potential. Leadership Potential Is Central to the Fellowship The Archbishop Tutu Fellowship is specifically aimed at the next generation of African leaders . Therefore, simply having a successful career may not be enough. Candidates should be able to demonstrate evidence of leadership potential. This may include: Leading organisations Building successful businesses Driving institutional reforms Developing innovative initiatives Leading social movements Creating community programmes Influencing policy Building partnerships Improving systems Mentoring others Advancing social justice Promoting economic development Addressing environmental challenges Creating opportunities for other people The strongest candidates are likely to be individuals whose leadership extends beyond personal advancement and demonstrates wider social value. Contribution to Africa s Transformation AFLI s nomination form specifically asks how a candidate s leadership will contribute to the transformation of Africa and improve the lives of people on the continent. This makes the candidate s broader vision particularly important. A prospective candidate should be able to articulate: What major challenge they are addressing Why the challenge matters What they have already done What impact they have achieved What they hope to accomplish in the future How their leadership can contribute to broader African development The emphasis should be on measurable or observable impact wherever possible. The Fellowship Is Not Limited to One Career Path One of the strengths of the Archbishop Tutu Fellowship is its cross-sector approach. The programme seeks future leaders from all sectors of society . This means that a candidate does not necessarily need to work in government, politics or international development. A leader in business, technology, education, health, civil society, entrepreneurship, media, agriculture, science or another sector can potentially be considered. What matters is the combination of leadership potential, achievement, vision and commitment to positive change. The Fellowship s Leadership Network AFLI aims to create a network of high-potential African leaders who have participated in its programmes. The purpose of this network is to connect individuals who are expected to move into significant leadership positions over the next five to ten years. This network can provide an environment in which fellows can exchange ideas, develop relationships and collaborate across countries and professional sectors. The fellowship therefore has a longer-term objective that extends beyond the immediate programme activities. What Does the Programme Aim to Develop? The leadership learning activities are designed to strengthen selected candidates : Experiences Insights Leadership tools Confidence Professional and leadership networks Capacity to drive transformation The programme seeks to give participants practical leadership resources that they can apply within their organisations, communities and wider societies. Preparing for the Tutu Fellowship Nomination If you are a prospective candidate, the first step is not to complete an application yourself. Instead, you should identify an appropriate person who can nominate you. Potential nominators could include people who know your work and leadership closely, depending on their relationship with you. Before asking someone to nominate you, consider whether they can genuinely explain: How they know you What leadership they have observed What makes you exceptional What impact you have made Why you have the potential to become a major African leader A nomination from someone who knows your work deeply is likely to provide more meaningful insight than a nomination from someone who knows you only superficially. What Makes a Strong Nomination? A strong nomination should tell a convincing leadership story. It should answer questions such as: What problem has the candidate addressed? Describe the challenge or opportunity that motivated the candidate s leadership. What did the candidate do? Explain the candidate s specific role rather than describing a collective achievement without identifying the individual s contribution. What changed because of the candidate s leadership? Where possible, provide evidence of outcomes. Why is the candidate different? Explain what distinguishes the person from other capable professionals. What could the candidate achieve in the future? Describe the candidate s future leadership potential and how it could contribute to Africa. The Importance of Impact Impact is an important concept throughout the fellowship s nomination process. Candidates should therefore consider the difference their leadership has made. Impact can take many forms, including: People reached Jobs created Policies influenced Organisations transformed Communities served Innovations introduced Educational outcomes improved Health outcomes improved Environmental benefits Economic opportunities created Young people mentored Women and marginalised communities empowered The relevant evidence will depend on the candidate s sector. Application Guidance and Official Resources Prospective nominators and candidates should review the official AFLI resources before participating in the process. Useful resources include: Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship Programme Guidelines for Candidates Guidelines for Nominators Guidelines for Selectors Key Dates and Deadlines AFLI Contact Page African Leadership Institute The official programme website also provides information about subscribing to the AFLI mailing list for announcements concerning the fellowship and other AFLI programmes. Important Application and Nomination Tips Prospective candidates and nominators should keep the following points in mind: Do not self-nominate. Direct applications and self-nominations are not accepted. Secure permission first. A candidate should know about and approve their nomination. Read the nomination guidance carefully. Submit the nomination early. The September 20 deadline is a hard deadline. Do not submit multiple nominations. The person should be able to provide meaningful insight into the candidate s leadership. Prepare for the formal application. Candidates who progress beyond screening should be ready to complete the next stage quickly. Choose referees early. Recommendation letters have a firm October 25 deadline. Focus on impact.
