title: NGA Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field: Paid U.S. Federal Internship Applications Open
summary: Applications are now open for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field , a paid opportunity for eligible college and university students interested in government contracting, procurement, acquisition management, finance, business administration, supply chain management, public administration, law, and related fields. The internship provides selected students with practical exposure to the full lifecycle of U.S. government acquisitions while working within the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, commonly known as NGA. Positions are available in Springfield, Virginia, and St. Louis, Missouri , and the advertised annual salary range across the applicable NGA pay bands and locations is $27,108 to $101,097 . The internship is not telework eligible, and participants should expect to work at their assigned NGA location. The application window opened on August 31, 2026 , and closes on September 30, 2026 . NGA states that vacancy announcements close at 11:59 p.m. EDT on the closing date , so applicants should submit their complete online applications before that time. About the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency is both a U.S. intelligence agency and a combat support agency. It is responsible for providing geospatial intelligence, commonly known as GEOINT, to support U.S. national security, defense, intelligence, navigation, and other government missions. NGA describes itself as a world leader in providing timely, relevant, accurate, and actionable geospatial intelligence. Its work supports the U.S. Intelligence Community and Department of Defense and involves the analysis and integration of imagery, geospatial information, data, and intelligence. The agency is headquartered in Springfield, Virginia , and also maintains major facilities in Missouri and other locations. Approximately 14,500 civilian, military, and contractor personnel work across NGA locations and supporting assignments worldwide. For students, an NGA internship therefore provides more than general workplace experience. Interns operate within a national-security environment and gain exposure to professional processes used by a major U.S. federal intelligence and defense-support organization. About the Summer 2027 Contracts Career Field Internship The Summer 2027 College Internship in the Contracts Career Field is particularly relevant to students interested in how the federal government purchases goods and services and manages complex contractual relationships. NGA explains that its Contracts Career Field helps procure the supplies and services required for the agency to accomplish its global mission. Interns can gain practical exposure to the functions performed by Contract Specialists , professionals responsible for planning acquisitions, evaluating proposals, negotiating agreements, awarding contracts, and ensuring contractors comply with contractual terms and conditions. The internship can therefore be highly relevant to students considering careers in: Government procurement Federal contracting Acquisition management Supply chain management Business administration Finance Public administration Contract management Pre-law or legal studies Commercial management Vendor and supplier management Government operations Defense acquisition Public-sector financial and commercial management What Interns Will Learn The internship is structured to expose students to the full lifecycle of government acquisitions . Although individual assignments will depend on NGA s operational and mission requirements, interns may gain experience in several important areas. 1. Acquisition Planning Interns may learn how government agencies identify procurement requirements and develop plans for acquiring necessary goods and services. This can involve understanding customer requirements, determining acquisition approaches, reviewing market information, and considering the most appropriate procurement strategy. 2. Development of Acquisition Strategies Students may assist or observe professionals developing strategies for acquiring products and services. An acquisition strategy considers issues such as requirements, procurement methods, competition, timelines, risks, contract structure, and expected outcomes. For students interested in supply chain management or procurement, this exposure can provide an important understanding of how large public-sector acquisitions are planned. 3. Vendor Proposal Evaluation Interns may learn how proposals submitted by vendors are evaluated. Proposal evaluation is a central component of government contracting because federal agencies must select contractors using defined procedures and evaluation criteria. Students can therefore gain exposure to structured commercial evaluation and government decision-making processes. 4. Contract Negotiation and Award The internship can provide insight into how government Contract Specialists negotiate with vendors and award contracts. Contract negotiations may involve issues such as pricing, contractual terms, deliverables, schedules, compliance requirements, and responsibilities. This experience can be particularly valuable to students studying business, finance, procurement, public administration, or law. 5. Contract Administration Awarding a contract is only one part of the procurement lifecycle. After award, government agencies must ensure that contractors fulfill their obligations. Interns may learn how contracts are administered to ensure compliance with applicable contractual terms and conditions. Internship Locations The announcement identifies vacancies in two locations: Springfield, Virginia and St. Louis, Missouri The USAJOBS announcement shows one vacancy in each location. The opportunity is not telework eligible , meaning applicants should be prepared to work physically at the assigned location. Relocation expenses are also listed as not reimbursed , so candidates who live outside these areas should carefully consider potential temporary housing, relocation, transportation, and living costs. Salary for the NGA Summer 2027 Internship USAJOBS publishes an overall annual salary range of: $27,108–$101,097 per year The applicable pay scale is listed as IA 01–02 . Because federal pay differs by pay band and geographic locality, compensation varies according to the location and the level at which the candidate is appointed. Published 2026 ranges associated with this particular recruitment include: Springfield / Washington, D.C. Locality Band 1: $30,249–$75,059 annually Band 2: $57,736–$101,097 annually St. Louis Locality Band 1: $27,108–$67,264 annually Band 2: $51,740–$90,597 annually. Applicants should understand that these are pay-band ranges rather than a guarantee that every intern will receive the maximum salary. Actual compensation will depend on NGA s placement determination and the candidate s applicable qualifications. Who Should Consider the Contracts Career Field? NGA specifically identifies several academic areas that align strongly with the Contracts Career Field. Students majoring in the following subjects may find the internship particularly relevant: Business Administration Supply Chain Management Finance Pre-Law Public Administration These are examples of suitable majors rather than the only educational backgrounds mentioned in the broader student eligibility requirements. Students interested in procurement, commercial operations, government contracting, business analysis, strategic problem-solving, financial management, public-sector administration, or acquisition policy may also find the professional experience especially valuable. Mandatory Eligibility Requirements Applicants should review the mandatory requirements carefully because failure to satisfy even one core condition can make an application ineligible. Minimum Age Applicants must be at least: 18 years old at the time of application. Current Student Status Candidates must currently be enrolled at least part-time in an accredited two-year or four-year college or university program. Eligible levels include: Associate degree Bachelor s degree Graduate degree Postgraduate degree Applicants must have an anticipated graduation date of October 2027 or later . Students who are expected to graduate before October 2027 are generally not eligible unless they have already been accepted into and enrolled in a subsequent qualifying degree program. This requirement is important because the internship is designed specifically for individuals who will continue to hold qualifying student status. GPA Requirement Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of: 3.0 or higher The GPA must appear on the most recent transcript uploaded with the application. Freshmen who do not yet have an established college GPA may initially provide appropriate enrollment documentation, but they will later need to demonstrate that they achieved at least a 3.0 GPA for the relevant semester. NGA states that offers may be rescinded if the required GPA is not subsequently achieved or verified. Proof of Current Enrollment Is Mandatory Although the USAJOBS required-documents summary displays None, the detailed vacancy instructions explicitly state that applicants must upload proof of current enrollment . Applicants should therefore follow the more specific instruction in the announcement. Students are required to provide their most recent unofficial transcript , showing: Date University information GPA Freshmen may submit a letter of enrollment from their university instead of a transcript where appropriate. Failure to provide this proof of enrollment can result in disqualification. Applicants who are ultimately accepted will also be required to provide an official transcript to NGA Student Programs after completion of the relevant semester. Communication Skills Requirement Applicants need experience providing clear verbal updates or explanations of routine information . This experience may have been acquired through: University presentations Group projects Employment Volunteer activities Student organizations Academic research Internships Professional or community activities Candidates should make sure their NGA resume provides specific examples rather than merely stating that they possess good communication skills. Problem-Solving and Data-Gathering Experience Candidates are also expected to demonstrate experience identifying and gathering information needed to resolve routine problems. This competency could potentially be demonstrated through coursework, research projects, employment, student activities, internships, or other relevant experiences. Applicants should emphasize situations in which they: Identified a problem Determined what information was required Collected or analyzed relevant information Reached a conclusion Recommended or implemented an appropriate solution The announcement specifically instructs applicants to use concrete examples and outcomes when demonstrating their qualifications. Artificial Intelligence Knowledge The current USAJOBS posting also identifies experience explaining fundamental artificial intelligence concepts and/or technologies used for routine tasks among the qualification criteria. Students who have used or studied AI applications should therefore consider demonstrating their knowledge clearly and accurately in their application where relevant. Examples could include academic exposure to: Generative AI Machine learning fundamentals AI-enabled research tools Data analytics Automation Responsible use of AI AI-assisted business processes Applicants should not exaggerate their expertise. The strongest approach is to provide a genuine example showing that they understand basic AI concepts and can explain them clearly. U.S. Citizenship Requirement One of the most important eligibility restrictions is that U.S. citizenship is required . Because NGA operates in the intelligence and national-security environment and the internship requires access eligibility for highly classified information, international students who are not U.S. citizens should not assume they qualify merely because they are studying at a U.S. university. The vacancy specifically identifies U.S. citizenship as a condition of employment. Security Clearance Requirement Applicants must be capable of obtaining and retaining a: Top Secret security clearance with Sensitive Compartmented Information access, commonly referred to as Top Secret/SCI. The security process is an important aspect of employment with NGA. Selected candidates are also subject to a Counterintelligence Polygraph examination and drug testing. Maintaining the required security eligibility is not simply an initial hiring requirement. Employees who require SCI access must continue to satisfy applicable security requirements throughout their NGA service. Drug Testing The announcement states that designated or random drug testing is required. Applicants must therefore be prepared to comply with federal and NGA drug-testing requirements as a condition of employment. Security Financial Disclosure Employees holding SCI access while under NGA cognizance may be required to submit an annual Security Financial Disclosure Report, SF-714 . The purpose of this requirement is to support continuing assessment of eligibility for access to sensitive national-security information. Failure to comply may affect continued access to classified information or secured facilities. Work Schedule and Travel The USAJOBS announcement identifies the work schedule as full-time . Travel is listed as: Not required Telework is also listed as: Not eligible Relocation expenses are: Not reimbursed. Students considering the position should therefore plan carefully for the practical requirements associated with spending the internship period in Springfield, Virginia, or St. Louis, Missouri. Federal Employment Classification The position falls under occupational series: 0099 – General Student Trainee and is within the Excepted Service . The applicable pay bands are IA 01–02. The announcement also notes that NGA operates under the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System , or DCIPS, for relevant civilian positions. Important Note About the Appointment Description Applicants may notice an apparent inconsistency in the USAJOBS announcement. The position is repeatedly described by NGA and related postings as the Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field , and the duties are expressly framed as an internship. However, the USAJOBS overview currently displays the appointment type as Permanent. Candidates should therefore rely on the official NGA application process for final confirmation of the precise appointment mechanics and employment duration rather than assuming that the Permanent field converts the Summer 2027 internship into an indefinite regular position. Resume Requirements Applicants must use the NGA resume builder . The vacancy specifically states that resumes must be limited to: Two pages. This is an important instruction. Applicants should not simply upload a lengthy general-purpose resume without checking NGA s prescribed process. A strong resume should directly address the mandatory qualification criteria and use specific examples demonstrating relevant experience. Candidates should highlight: Educational enrollment GPA Expected graduation date Presentation and communication experience Problem identification Data gathering and analysis AI knowledge or experience Business or procurement exposure Leadership Academic projects Relevant employment Internships Volunteer experience Quantifiable achievements NGA advises applicants to demonstrate the level and complexity of work they have performed and to include specific examples and results. Is a Cover Letter Required? A cover letter is not mandatory , but NGA recommends submitting one. Applicants are given the option to attach a cover letter during the online application process. Because this is a competitive intelligence-community internship, a focused cover letter can help an applicant explain why the Contracts Career Field aligns with their academic studies and career plans. A strong letter could address: Interest in NGA s mission Interest in federal acquisitions Relevant academic background Problem-solving capabilities Communication skills Interest in public service Understanding of government contracting Career goals The letter should complement the resume rather than simply repeat it. How Candidates Will Be Evaluated NGA uses a multi-stage applicant evaluation process. First, applications are reviewed against the mandatory qualification criteria . Candidates who meet those requirements may then be evaluated by an expert or panel of experts using additional qualification criteria to identify the best-qualified applicants. Those considered best qualified may subsequently be invited to participate in an interview process . Meeting the minimum requirements therefore does not guarantee selection. Veterans Preference As a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System position in the Excepted Service, applicable veterans preference procedures may apply. External applicants claiming veterans preference must appropriately identify their eligibility in accordance with the vacancy instructions and applicable Department of Defense procedures. Equal Employment Opportunity NGA states that applicants will be considered without regard to factors including: Race Color Religion Sex National origin Age Marital status Disability Sexual orientation The agency also provides a process for requesting reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities during the recruitment and hiring process. How to Apply for the NGA Summer 2027 Internship Applications must be submitted electronically through NGA s online recruitment process. NGA states clearly that only electronic submissions will be accepted. Applicants should: Review the entire USAJOBS announcement carefully. Confirm that they satisfy the U.S. citizenship requirement. Confirm that they will be at least 18 when applying. Confirm qualifying college or university enrollment. Verify that their graduation date is October 2027 or later, unless continuing into another eligible program. Ensure that their GPA is at least 3.0. Obtain an up-to-date unofficial transcript showing enrollment details and GPA. Prepare a targeted two-page resume using the NGA resume builder. Consider preparing a focused cover letter. Complete all questions in the NGA online application. Upload the required enrollment evidence. Review the entire application before submitting. Submit before the September 30, 2026 deadline. Applicants can subsequently follow the status of their application through NGA s online application system. Application Deadline The application period for the NGA Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field is: Opening date: August 31, 2026 Closing date: September 30, 2026 The NGA announcement states that applications close at: 11:59 p.m. EDT on the closing date. Applicants are strongly advised not to wait until the final hours because transcript uploads, resume preparation, account issues, or technical problems could prevent timely submission. Why Students Should Consider This Opportunity This internship can provide valuable exposure to an area of the federal government that is rarely experienced through ordinary university coursework. Federal acquisitions involve large-scale purchasing, regulatory requirements, vendor relationships, financial analysis, negotiation, risk management, strategic planning, and contract administration. Students selected for the Contracts Career Field may therefore develop transferable professional skills relevant to careers in: Federal government Defense Intelligence Procurement Finance Consulting Supply chain management Contract management Public administration Commercial management Working inside NGA also provides exposure to an organization operating at the intersection of national security, intelligence, technology, data, and government administration. Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application Competition for federal intelligence-community internships can be significant, so candidates should avoid submitting a generic application. Applicants should carefully map their experience against each mandatory qualification. For example, instead of writing: Good communication skills a candidate could explain that they presented findings from a semester-long research project to a class of 30 students and answered questions about the methodology and conclusions. Instead of stating: Good problem-solving skills the applicant could describe a project in which they identified missing data, collected information from several sources, evaluated alternatives, and produced a recommendation. Students should also ensure that their graduation date and GPA can be immediately verified from their submitted documentation. Most importantly, applicants should be accurate and truthful throughout the process because the role involves a high-level federal security investigation. Conclusion The NGA Summer 2027 College Internship – Contracts Career Field offers eligible U.S. college and university students an opportunity to gain paid, practical experience inside one of the United States principal intelligence and combat-support agencies. With positions available in Springfield, Virginia, and St. Louis, Missouri , students can gain exposure to government acquisitions, procurement strategy, proposal evaluation, contract negotiation, contract award, and contract administration. The internship is particularly relevant to students studying Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Pre-Law, Public Administration , and related disciplines. Applicants must satisfy strict eligibility requirements, including being at least 18 years old, a U.S. citizen, currently enrolled at least part-time in an accredited degree program, maintaining a GPA of at least 3.0, and generally having a graduation date of October 2027 or later . Candidates must also be able to obtain and maintain the required Top Secret/SCI security clearance and comply with applicable polygraph and drug-testing requirements. The application deadline is September 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EDT . Students who meet the requirements should prepare their transcript and targeted two-page NGA resume early and submit through the official online application system well before the deadline. title: Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7: Apply for a 12-Week Virtual Mental Health Leadership Fellowship in Africa
summary: The Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7 is inviting applications from emerging and established changemakers who want to deepen their understanding of mental health and develop practical leadership skills to address mental health challenges within their communities. The 12-week virtual fellowship brings together participants interested in mental health, community development, advocacy, education, healthcare, research, humanitarian work and related fields. Designed with a strong focus on African realities while incorporating African and global perspectives, the fellowship goes beyond basic mental health awareness. Participants will engage with mental health experts, practitioners, researchers and leaders while exploring subjects ranging from community mental health and lived experience to neuropsychology, learning how the brain, mind, environment and society interact to influence wellbeing. The programme also places a strong emphasis on turning knowledge into community action. At the end of the fellowship, participants will develop and implement a Community Impact Capstone Project designed to address a mental health challenge and create measurable benefits within their communities. About the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship The Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship is a 12-week virtual leadership and learning programme intended for people who want to become more effective changemakers in the mental health space. Rather than limiting participants to theoretical discussions about mental health, the fellowship is structured around learning, leadership, community engagement and practical action. Participants will be exposed to perspectives from: Mental health experts Practitioners Researchers Leaders People with lived experience Diverse communities and professional backgrounds The fellowship examines mental health through both African and global perspectives , giving participants an opportunity to understand mental health challenges within the broader social, cultural and environmental contexts in which people live. This approach is particularly relevant to individuals who recognize that mental wellbeing cannot be addressed solely through clinical interventions. Community structures, education, social environments, policy, culture, advocacy and access to information can all influence mental health outcomes. What Participants Will Learn The fellowship covers a broad range of mental health-related themes. These include: Community Mental Health Participants will explore mental health from a community perspective, considering how communities can better identify, discuss and respond to mental health challenges. Lived Experience The programme recognizes lived experience as an important form of knowledge and leadership. Participants will have opportunities to engage with perspectives shaped by real-world experiences of mental health. Neuropsychology The fellowship also introduces participants to neuropsychology and the relationship between the brain, mind and behaviour. Learning and Wellbeing Participants will develop a deeper understanding of how learning, environments and social conditions can influence wellbeing. African and Global Perspectives A central feature of the programme is its grounding in African realities while drawing on broader global perspectives. This can help participants consider how mental health approaches can be adapted to the contexts in which their communities operate. From Mental Health Awareness to Community Action One of the defining features of the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship is its focus on moving beyond awareness. The programme is designed to help participants understand how to act on mental health challenges within their communities. Throughout the fellowship, participants can strengthen their ability to: Identify mental health challenges. Understand the needs of their communities. Engage with different perspectives. Develop practical approaches to mental health challenges. Communicate mental health information effectively. Build networks with other changemakers. Apply learning to community-level action. Develop initiatives capable of reaching people beyond the fellowship itself. This practical orientation culminates in the Community Impact Capstone Project. Community Impact Capstone Project The Community Impact Capstone Project is a central component of the fellowship. Fellows will take knowledge gained during the programme and apply it to a real mental health issue affecting their communities. The project is intended to create a tangible community impact rather than remaining solely as an academic or theoretical exercise. Previous fellows have reportedly undertaken initiatives including: Community dialogues Radio programmes Mental health awareness campaigns School-based interventions Outreach activities The fellowship seeks to create a ripple effect in which one participant s knowledge and leadership can reach and positively influence many other people. For Cohort 7, applicants will need to demonstrate that they can design and implement a project that benefits their community. The selection criteria specifically consider the strength and feasibility of the proposed project, including its potential to positively influence at least 200 community members . Who Should Apply for the Nivishe Fellowship? The programme is seeking passionate individuals committed to addressing mental health disparities and promoting mental wellbeing. Applicants should ideally demonstrate one or more of the following characteristics: A commitment to reducing mental health disparities. An interest in improving mental wellbeing in their communities. Current or potential leadership responsibilities. An interest in community development. Experience or interest in advocacy. Experience or interest in education. Experience or interest in healthcare. Experience or interest in research. Experience or interest in humanitarian work. A desire to create positive social change. An appreciation for diversity and inclusion. Willingness to learn from different perspectives and lived experiences. Formal mental health employment or professional experience is not required . The application specifically states that leadership and commitment to community wellbeing can be demonstrated in different ways. Age Requirements Applicants must be 18 years or older . The fellowship is primarily aimed at young leaders between 18 and 35 years old . However, people above 35 should not automatically rule themselves out. The programme specifically encourages applicants over 35 who have a strong track record of: Community leadership Advocacy Social impact This makes the opportunity accessible to both emerging young leaders and more experienced changemakers who can demonstrate meaningful community impact. Professional and Sectoral Backgrounds The application form accommodates applicants from a wide range of professional and community sectors. Relevant sectors include: Mental health Healthcare Education Research Humanitarian response Community development Advocacy and activism Government and public service Youth leadership Faith-based organizations Media and communications Private sector Other related fields This broad range demonstrates that the fellowship is not exclusively intended for psychologists, psychiatrists or other clinical mental health professionals. Professionals working in communication, education, public service, youth leadership, community development and other sectors can also be relevant applicants if they have a genuine interest in mental health and community impact. Eligibility Requirements To be considered for the fellowship, applicants should meet the following requirements: 1. Be at Least 18 Years Old The minimum age is 18. 2. Demonstrate Commitment to Mental Health Applicants should demonstrate a genuine commitment to addressing mental health disparities and promoting mental wellbeing. 3. Have an Interest in a Relevant Field Applicants may be involved in or interested in mental health, community development, advocacy, education, healthcare, research, humanitarian work or related areas. 4. Demonstrate Leadership Potential Applicants should hold or aspire to leadership positions and demonstrate the ability to influence positive change in their communities or institutions. 5. Value Diversity and Inclusion Applicants should be willing to learn from people with different identities, cultures, professions and lived experiences. 6. Have Reliable Internet Access Because the fellowship is conducted virtually, applicants need access to a computer and reliable internet connection. 7. Commit to a Community Project Applicants should be able to design and implement a Community Impact Capstone Project that applies their fellowship learning to benefit their community. Selection Criteria Applications will be evaluated against several criteria. 1. Leadership Potential and Community Impact The selection team will look for evidence of leadership experience, initiative and commitment to creating positive change. Applicants should therefore explain not only what positions they have held but also what they have actually done and the results their actions produced. 2. Commitment to Mental Health Advancement Applicants should demonstrate a clear interest in mental health, wellbeing or related social issues. This commitment can be demonstrated through professional activities, volunteering, advocacy, community initiatives, education, research or other relevant experiences. 3. Availability and Engagement The fellowship requires active participation. Applicants will be assessed on their ability to participate in: Fellowship sessions Collaborative activities Assignments Group discussions 4. Lived Experience and Personal Motivation The programme recognizes lived experience as a valuable source of expertise. Applicants who have personal, family, professional or community experiences that have shaped their interest in mental health may choose to explain how those experiences influence their commitment to mental health advocacy and systems change. However, this section is optional. 5. Diversity and Inclusion The fellowship aims to create a cohort representing diverse: Identities Geographies Cultures Professions Lived experiences This means the selection process is not based solely on professional credentials but also considers the diversity of perspectives applicants can bring to the cohort. 6. Community Impact Capstone Proposal The proposed capstone project is another important part of the selection process. Applicants should present a project that is: Relevant to a genuine community mental health challenge Practical Feasible Capable of implementation Designed to create meaningful impact The selection criteria indicate that the project should have potential to positively influence at least 200 community members . Fellowship Schedule and Time Commitment The Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship will run for 12 weeks . Sessions will take place: Every Saturday, from 10:00 AM to 12:30 PM EAT. Selected fellows are expected to attend weekly virtual sessions throughout the programme. In addition to the weekly sessions, fellows should expect to commit approximately six hours per month to assignments, collaborative activities and group discussions. Participants should therefore assess their schedules carefully before applying and ensure that they can maintain consistent participation throughout the entire programme. Expectations for Selected Fellows Those selected for Cohort 7 will be expected to: Attend weekly virtual fellowship sessions for 12 weeks. Commit approximately six additional hours per month to assignments and collaborative activities. Participate actively in peer learning. Engage in networking opportunities. Communicate effectively in English. Complete the required assignments. Design and implement a Community Impact Capstone Project. Address a mental health issue relevant to their community. Contribute to the Nivishe Fellowship Network after completing the programme. Continue advancing mental health leadership beyond the fellowship period. Language Requirement The fellowship will be conducted in English . Selected fellows are therefore expected to be proficient in English and able to participate effectively in virtual sessions, discussions, assignments and collaborative activities. Application Questions The application requires candidates to provide detailed responses demonstrating their motivation, understanding of mental health, leadership experience and plans for community impact. Question 1: Personal Motivation and Commitment Applicants will be asked why they want to join the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship and how the programme aligns with their personal, professional or community leadership goals. The response should be between 100 and 200 words . Candidates should use this section to communicate their motivation and explain how the fellowship could help them grow as changemakers. Question 2: Mental Health Understanding and Community Context Applicants will be asked to explain what good mental health means to them and identify pressing mental health challenges affecting their community, institution or the population they work with. The response should be 100–200 words . This question provides an opportunity to demonstrate understanding of mental health within a specific community context. Question 3: Leadership, Experience and Impact Applicants will need to describe their current or previous involvement in areas such as: Mental health Community development Advocacy Education Healthcare Research Related areas They should also explain the impact they have made and the leadership lessons they have gained. The response should be 100–200 words . Importantly, formal mental health experience is not mandatory. Applicants can demonstrate leadership and commitment to community wellbeing through different types of experiences. Question 4: Community Impact Capstone Project Applicants will be asked to propose a mental health initiative they would like to implement during the fellowship. The response should be 150–300 words . Applicants should describe: The community mental health challenge they want to address The proposed initiative The community they hope to reach The expected impact Possible approaches include awareness campaigns, community dialogues, radio programmes, school activities, digital campaigns, support groups, workplace initiatives, research dissemination and advocacy efforts. The application also notes that project ideas may evolve during the fellowship as fellows gain additional knowledge and mentorship. Question 5: Community Reach and Ripple Effect Applicants must explain how they intend to share knowledge, skills and networks gained through the fellowship with people beyond themselves. The response should be 100–200 words . Candidates can discuss how they plan to engage: Community members Organizations Institutions Professional networks Youth groups Other relevant stakeholders The purpose is to demonstrate how participation in the fellowship can produce a wider community impact rather than benefiting only the individual fellow. Question 6: Lived Experience and Perspective Applicants may optionally discuss personal, family, professional or community experiences that have shaped their interest in mental health. This is an optional question requiring a response of 100–200 words . Applicants should only share what they are comfortable discussing. The programme recognizes lived experience as a valuable form of expertise and leadership. Question 7: Commitment Statement Applicants must indicate whether they can commit fully to the fellowship s requirements. The programme requires: Weekly attendance Active participation Assignment completion Community Impact Capstone Project implementation Applicants who answer yes must briefly explain how they will ensure their participation throughout the 12-week programme. The response should be 50–100 words . How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants should approach the application as an opportunity to demonstrate not just interest in mental health but also their potential to create community-level impact. Demonstrate Genuine Motivation Clearly explain why mental health matters to you and why this particular fellowship is relevant to your goals. Connect Your Experience to Community Impact Whether your background is in communications, education, healthcare, advocacy, research, government, youth leadership or community development, explain how your experience has helped you contribute to positive change. Identify a Specific Community Challenge For the capstone project, avoid proposing an overly broad initiative. Identify a specific challenge and explain how your project could address it. Think About Measurable Impact Because the fellowship emphasizes community reach, applicants should think about how their proposed project could reach and positively influence at least 200 people. Demonstrate Leadership Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a senior job title. Applicants can demonstrate leadership through volunteering, community organizing, advocacy, educational initiatives, youth engagement, research or other forms of social impact. Show Commitment The programme requires consistent participation over 12 weeks. Applicants should demonstrate that they have considered the time commitment and can participate fully. Application Timeline The application timeline for Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7 is: Applications open: September 9, 2026 Applications close: September 18, 2026 Fellowship sessions: Every Saturday, 10:00 AM–12:30 PM EAT Fellowship duration: 12 weeks The application deadline is therefore September 18, 2026 . Application Support Nivishe states that it is committed to making the application process accessible and inclusive. Applicants who experience challenges completing or submitting the application, or who require reasonable accommodation because of a disability, language barrier or other circumstances, can contact the Nivishe team for support. The organization states that it will make efforts to assist applicants and provide an equitable opportunity to apply. How to Apply Interested candidates should complete the official Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7 Application Form and provide the information and written responses requested in the application. Applicants should carefully review each question, observe the specified word limits and ensure that their responses clearly demonstrate motivation, leadership, mental health understanding and potential community impact. For application support, the fellowship provides the following email address: partnerships@nivishefoundation.org APPLY HERE Why You Should Consider the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship The fellowship can be particularly valuable for emerging leaders who want to combine personal development with practical community impact. Key opportunities include: Deepen your understanding of mental health: Explore mental health through African and global perspectives. Develop leadership skills: Strengthen your capacity to lead initiatives and influence positive change. Learn from experts: Engage with mental health experts, practitioners, researchers and leaders. Build an international and diverse network: Connect with people from different professional, cultural and geographic backgrounds. Gain practical experience: Apply fellowship learning through a Community Impact Capstone Project. Reach your community: Develop an initiative capable of benefiting at least 200 community members. Strengthen communication and advocacy: Learn how to translate knowledge into activities that engage communities. Continue beyond the fellowship: Join the growing Nivishe Fellowship Network and continue contributing to mental health leadership. Important Things Applicants Should Remember Before submitting an application, candidates should make sure they understand the fellowship s key requirements. The fellowship is: Virtual 12 weeks long Conducted in English Scheduled every Saturday from 10:00 AM to 12:30 PM EAT Designed for participants aged 18 and above Primarily focused on young leaders aged 18–35 Open to older applicants with relevant leadership and social-impact experience Based on active participation Inclusive of diverse professional and community backgrounds Built around a Community Impact Capstone Project Applicants should also ensure that they have reliable internet access and the ability to participate consistently in online sessions. Visit HERE for more information about the Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7. Conclusion The Nivishe Mental Health Fellowship Cohort 7 presents an opportunity for emerging and established changemakers to develop deeper knowledge of mental health while building the leadership and practical skills needed to create meaningful community impact. The programme stands out because it does not focus solely on mental health awareness. Instead, it combines expert-led learning, diverse perspectives, leadership development, networking and practical community action. Through the Community Impact Capstone Project , fellows are expected to transform what they learn into an initiative that addresses a real mental health challenge and has the potential to reach at least 200 community members. The fellowship is particularly suitable for young leaders aged 18–35 , while experienced applicants above 35 with strong records in community leadership, advocacy or social impact are also encouraged to apply. Applicants can come from a wide range of sectors, and formal mental health experience is not mandatory. With applications opening on September 9, 2026, and closing on September 18, 2026 , interested candidates should begin preparing their application responses early. A strong application should clearly communicate the applicant s motivation, leadership experience, understanding of their community s mental health challenges and a realistic vision for creating a wider ripple effect through the fellowship. title: Royal Commonwealth Society Recruitment 2026: Apply for the Digital Communications and Public Affairs Officer Role in London
summary: The Royal Commonwealth Society (RCS) is currently accepting applications for an exciting professional opportunity in London, United Kingdom. The organisation is recruiting a Digital Communications and Public Affairs Officer to support its growing communications, digital engagement, public affairs and stakeholder outreach activities. This full-time position presents an excellent opportunity for communications professionals who are interested in international affairs, digital storytelling, youth engagement, public affairs and the Commonwealth. The successful candidate will contribute to some of the Royal Commonwealth Society’s most visible programmes and events while helping the organisation expand its digital presence and connect with audiences across the Commonwealth and beyond. The position is based in London, United Kingdom , with a salary of £27,000 to £29,000 per year . The Society states that flexible working arrangements may be considered for the right candidate. Applications must be received by the opening of business on Tuesday, 29 September 2026 . About the Royal Commonwealth Society The Royal Commonwealth Society is a long-established organisation dedicated to improving the lives and prospects of people across the Commonwealth. Founded in 1868 , the Society operates as a non-partisan organisation independent of governments. Its work brings together political and diplomatic representatives, civil society organisations, businesses, young people and other stakeholders from across the Commonwealth. The RCS works across the Commonwealth’s 56 member countries , focusing particularly on three interconnected areas: education, equality and inclusion, and the environment . Its wider mission is to connect, convene and equip people to advance Commonwealth values and contribute to a fairer world for Commonwealth citizens. The Society also delivers and supports internationally recognised initiatives, programmes and events involving young people, governments, diplomatic representatives and civil society. Its Strategic Plan for 2025–2030 places particular emphasis on strengthening collaboration across the Commonwealth, developing young leaders and advancing progress towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals through initiatives connected with education, equality and environmental sustainability. Why the Royal Commonwealth Society Is Expanding Its Digital Communications The recruitment comes at an important period for the Royal Commonwealth Society. The organisation will celebrate its 160th anniversary in 2028 , and it is developing an ambitious programme of communications and digital engagement aimed at introducing the Society and the wider Commonwealth to new audiences around the world. One of the major initiatives associated with this expansion is Digital Commonwealth Day , which is intended to complement the Society’s annual Commonwealth Day Celebration at Westminster Abbey. Digital content, video, social media and online storytelling are expected to play an increasingly important role in allowing audiences outside London to engage with Commonwealth Day activities and other programmes. The new Digital Communications and Public Affairs Officer will therefore have a significant operational role in implementing this expanding digital strategy. About the Digital Communications and Public Affairs Officer Position The Digital Communications and Public Affairs Officer will be responsible for supporting and delivering the Royal Commonwealth Society’s day-to-day communications and digital activities while also contributing to public affairs and stakeholder engagement. This is not solely an administrative communications position. It is designed as a practical and creative role involving written content, social media management, website administration, photography, video, digital campaigns, events and stakeholder communications. Candidates should therefore be comfortable moving between different communication formats and audiences. The position will involve contributing to several major Royal Commonwealth Society programmes, including Commonwealth Day, Digital Commonwealth Day, the Queen’s Commonwealth Writing Competition, the Commonwealth Youth Photography Competition and preparations for the Society’s 160th anniversary. The Queen’s Commonwealth Writing Competition itself is one of the Society’s most established education initiatives and is recognised by the RCS as the world’s oldest international writing competition for schools, having been delivered by the organisation since 1883. Key Responsibilities The successful candidate will undertake a broad range of communications, digital engagement, public affairs and events responsibilities. These include: Developing engaging communications and digital content for the RCS website, social media platforms, email communications and other digital channels; managing website content including news, blogs, campaign materials and events; creating and scheduling professional content for LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and X; producing short-form videos, photography, graphics and other visual material; using Canva and similar digital communication tools; producing the Society s monthly newsletter; capturing interviews, photographs and videos during events; creating stories highlighting young people, partners and RCS initiatives; monitoring digital performance and using analytics to improve engagement; identifying emerging platforms and communication opportunities; supporting communications surrounding Commonwealth Day and Digital Commonwealth Day; producing pre-event, live-event and post-event digital content; working with youth networks, Commonwealth partners and stakeholders; supporting communications for the RCS s 160th anniversary; assisting with major programmes and events; contributing to briefings, speeches and correspondence; developing relationships with external organisations and Commonwealth stakeholders; and representing the RCS at appropriate events and networking opportunities. Commonwealth Day and Digital Commonwealth Day A particularly significant element of the role will involve communications surrounding the annual Commonwealth Day Celebration at Westminster Abbey . Commonwealth Day forms an important part of the RCS calendar and brings together participants and representatives connected with the Commonwealth. The successful applicant will assist in creating communications before, during and after the event while helping the Society expand participation through Digital Commonwealth Day. The Royal Commonwealth Society s wider convening role regularly brings together governments, diplomatic representatives, civil society, businesses and young people, meaning that communications surrounding these programmes can potentially reach diverse audiences across numerous regions and professional sectors. Essential Skills and Experience The Royal Commonwealth Society is looking for an individual with strong written and verbal communication abilities and excellent attention to detail. Applicants are expected to have relevant experience in areas such as communications, marketing, digital communications or public affairs. Strong practical experience with digital and social media content is particularly important. This includes experience creating short-form video and producing material suitable for public-facing digital channels. Candidates should also be comfortable managing websites and producing content for general audiences. Professional familiarity with major social media platforms is expected, alongside experience using design and content creation software such as Canva or equivalent tools . The successful applicant should be capable of managing multiple assignments and deadlines simultaneously while working creatively and proactively. Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills are also important because the position involves regular interaction with internal colleagues, partners, youth networks, diplomatic stakeholders and external organisations. An interest in areas such as international affairs, the Commonwealth, advocacy or youth engagement is specifically relevant to the position. UK Right-to-Work Requirement One particularly important eligibility condition should be carefully considered before applying. Applicants must have the right to live and work in the United Kingdom . The vacancy announcement does not state that visa sponsorship will be provided. International candidates should therefore not assume that being a citizen of a Commonwealth country automatically makes them eligible for employment. Candidates outside the United Kingdom should first establish whether they already possess an appropriate UK immigration or employment status permitting them to take up the position. Desirable Experience While not mandatory, candidates will be particularly competitive if they have experience working with website content management systems, especially Wix . Knowledge of video-editing software and digital analytics would also strengthen an application. Other useful backgrounds include experience designing digital campaigns, developing online communities, promoting youth-led programmes and supporting high-profile events involving external organisations or partners. Candidates who already understand the Commonwealth system or the mission and programmes of the Royal Commonwealth Society may also be able to demonstrate stronger alignment with the organisation. Applicants should also be aware that the position may occasionally require work outside normal working hours because of the nature of events, communications activities and programmes. Candidates should assess their ability to work from London and participate physically in major events and activities associated with the position. For example, rather than merely stating that they managed social media accounts, an applicant could explain how their campaign increased engagement, audience reach, followers or participation. The first interview is scheduled for 7 October 2026 , while the second interview is scheduled for 14 October 2026 . Both interview stages are expected to take place in person at Guildhall in the City of London . This is particularly important for applicants who are currently based outside London, as shortlisted candidates may need to make appropriate arrangements to attend the interviews physically. The Society also notes that because of capacity limitations, it cannot provide individual feedback to candidates who are not invited to interview. The strongest applications should clearly demonstrate practical communications experience, creativity, digital capability, writing ability, stakeholder engagement and genuine interest in the Society’s mission. Applicants should also ensure that any claims made about digital communications experience can be supported with specific examples, outcomes, campaigns, portfolios or measurable results where appropriate. Conclusion The Royal Commonwealth Society Digital Communications and Public Affairs Officer Recruitment 2026 represents a strong professional opportunity for candidates seeking experience at the intersection of communications, digital media, international affairs, youth engagement and public affairs. With an annual salary of £27,000–£29,000 , involvement in major Commonwealth programmes, and opportunities to contribute to initiatives such as Commonwealth Day, Digital Commonwealth Day and the RCS’s 160th anniversary programme, the position could provide valuable professional exposure within an internationally focused organisation. title: UNU-MERIT MMPAF Programme 2026: Apply for Online Training in Migration and Asylum Policy
summary: The Moving the Migration Policy Agenda Forward (MMPAF) Programme 2026 is an online capacity-building opportunity offered by the United Nations University – Maastricht Economic and Social Research Institute on Innovation and Technology (UNU-MERIT) for professionals involved in migration and asylum policy and management. The programme is particularly designed for government officials working in the fields of migration and asylum , while also providing an opportunity for other practitioners and students with an interest in migration and asylum policies to develop relevant knowledge and practical skills. Funded by the European Union (EU) through the Migration Partnership Facility (MPF) of the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD), the MMPAF programme provides intensive, tutor-led online learning focused on major migration policy issues. For 2026, participants can take part in two specialised courses: Irregular Migration and Migration and Development . Each course is delivered online over one full-time week and combines lectures, interactive learning, practical exercises and Problem-Based Learning (PBL). About the UNU-MERIT MMPAF Programme UNU-MERIT is an international research and training institute that forms part of the United Nations University system. Its work covers economic and social research, innovation, technology, development and public policy. The Moving the Migration Policy Agenda Forward (MMPAF) programme contributes to capacity development in migration management by giving participants the opportunity to strengthen their understanding of important migration policy challenges. Rather than relying exclusively on traditional lectures, the programme uses a combination of teaching and assessment approaches. Participants are expected to actively engage in online sessions, discussions, practical exercises and workshops. The programme places particular emphasis on Problem-Based Learning (PBL) , an approach that allows participants to work through practical policy-related challenges and apply concepts to real-world situations. MMPAF Programme 2026 Courses The 2026 programme consists of two separate online courses. Each course lasts one week and is delivered on a full-time basis. 1. Irregular Migration Dates: 23–27 November 2026 The Irregular Migration course will be taught by Dr. Lalaine Siruno . The course is intended to strengthen participants understanding of irregular migration and the policy challenges associated with managing migration movements. Through interactive learning and practical exercises, participants can explore migration policy issues and develop their ability to approach complex challenges from a policy and management perspective. 2. Migration and Development Dates: 30 November–4 December 2026 The Migration and Development course will be taught by Prof. Khalid Koser . This course focuses on the relationship between migration and development and provides participants with an opportunity to examine migration through a broader policy and development lens. The course is particularly relevant to professionals who need to understand how migration interacts with development policies, institutions and wider socioeconomic processes. How the MMPAF Courses Are Delivered Both courses are delivered entirely online , allowing selected participants to participate without travelling to a physical campus. However, the online format does not mean that the programme is self-paced. The courses are structured as intensive, full-time learning programmes. Each one-week course is divided into smaller learning blocks to make the programme structured and manageable. These learning blocks combine different forms of teaching and evaluation. Participants may be involved in: Online lectures Interactive sessions Practical exercises Problem-Based Learning activities Workshops Self-preparation and independent study Other tutor-led learning and evaluation activities The programme requires a significant time commitment. Participants are expected to dedicate approximately 40 hours per week to the course, including online contact hours and time spent preparing independently. Applicants should therefore ensure that they can make the necessary time available before applying. Who Can Apply for the MMPAF Programme? The MMPAF programme is primarily targeted at government officials and civil servants working in migration and/or asylum in the eligible countries and regions. The programme is also open to other practitioners and students who have an interest in migration and asylum policy, although the stated eligibility criteria specifically require applicants working as government officials in the relevant fields and eligible locations. Applicants should meet the following requirements: English Language Requirement Applicants must be fluent in spoken and written English . Because the programme is delivered online and involves interactive sessions, participants need to be comfortable communicating, listening, reading and writing in English. Academic Qualification Applicants must hold at least a Bachelor s degree . This means that a recognised undergraduate degree is the minimum academic qualification specified for the programme. Identification Document Applicants must provide a copy of a valid passport or identification document as part of their application. Applicants should therefore ensure that their identification document is valid and that they can provide a clear copy when submitting their application. Computer Skills Applicants must be sufficiently confident with computers to participate in an online education programme. Since the courses are delivered online and involve interactive sessions and practical activities, participants should be able to use the technology required for online learning. Professional Background The programme is specifically intended for government officials working in migration and/or asylum . Eligible officials must work in the relevant fields in one of the programme s designated geographical areas. Applicants who are government employees must also have full and written support from their employers confirming that they will not be expected to perform their normal work duties during the period of the MMPAF programme. This requirement is important because each course is full-time and requires approximately 40 hours of commitment per week. Eligible Countries and Regions The MMPAF programme is open to applicants from specific countries across the EU Southern Neighbourhood, Silk Route, Central Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia . EU Southern Neighbourhood Countries Eligible countries listed under this category are: Algeria Egypt Israel Jordan Lebanon Libya Morocco State of Palestine Syria Tunisia Silk Route Countries Eligible Silk Route countries include: Afghanistan Pakistan Iran Iraq Bangladesh Sub-Saharan African Countries Applicants from the following Sub-Saharan African countries are eligible: Burkina Faso Burundi Cabo Verde Cameroon Central African Republic Chad Côte d Ivoire Djibouti Ethiopia Ghana Guinea Guinea-Bissau Kenya Mali Mauritania Nigeria Rwanda Senegal Somalia The Gambia Uganda This makes the programme particularly relevant to migration and asylum professionals across a wide range of African countries. South Asian Countries The listed South Asian countries are: India Bangladesh Afghanistan Pakistan Central Asian Countries Eligible Central Asian countries include: Kazakhstan Kyrgyzstan Tajikistan Turkmenistan Uzbekistan Applicants should carefully check the official eligibility information before submitting an application, particularly where countries appear under more than one regional grouping in the programme s published list. Why the MMPAF Programme Is Valuable for Migration Professionals Migration and asylum policy involves complex economic, social, humanitarian, political and governance considerations. Professionals working in this area need the ability to understand policy challenges and respond to changing migration dynamics. The MMPAF programme provides an opportunity to strengthen this professional capacity through intensive, specialised training. Participants can benefit from: Exposure to specialised migration and asylum policy topics Tutor-led instruction from experienced academics and experts Interactive online learning Practical policy-oriented exercises Problem-Based Learning activities Opportunities to engage with other participants A structured full-time learning experience Greater understanding of irregular migration Greater understanding of the relationship between migration and development Skills that can support professional work in migration management and policy The practical emphasis of the programme can be particularly useful for professionals who need to apply migration concepts to real-world policy and administrative challenges. Full-Time Commitment and Employer Support One of the most important aspects applicants should consider is the programme s time requirement. Each course lasts one week and requires participants to dedicate 40 hours per week to the programme. This time commitment includes: Online contact and teaching sessions Interactive exercises Practical workshops Self-preparation Other programme-related learning activities Government officials applying to the programme must therefore secure written support from their employers confirming that they will be released from their regular work duties for the duration of the programme. Applicants should obtain this support before or as part of the application process so that they can demonstrate their ability to participate fully. MMPAF Programme 2026 Course Schedule The two courses are scheduled as follows: Course Dates Instructor Irregular Migration 23–27 November 2026 Dr. Lalaine Siruno Migration and Development 30 November–4 December 2026 Prof. Khalid Koser Both courses are conducted online. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the MMPAF Programme 2026 is 4 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST . Applicants are encouraged not to wait until the final day to submit their applications. Supporting documents should be prepared in advance, and applicants should make sure that all required information is complete before submission. Selection Notification Applicants can expect to receive notification of the selection outcome in mid-October 2026 . How to Apply for the MMPAF Programme Interested applicants should submit their details and all required supporting documents through the official online application portal provided by UNU-MERIT. The application process involves providing the information requested by the programme and submitting the necessary supporting documentation. Applicants should ensure that they: Confirm that they meet the eligibility requirements. Check that their country is included among the eligible locations. Confirm that they hold at least a Bachelor s degree. Ensure they are fluent in written and spoken English. Prepare a valid passport or identification document. Confirm that they have sufficient computer skills for online study. Obtain the required written employer support where applicable. Ensure they can commit approximately 40 hours during the relevant course week. Submit the completed application before the stated deadline. APPLY HERE Important Information for Prospective Applicants The MMPAF programme is not a casual or self-paced online course. It is a full-time, intensive capacity-building programme . Applicants should therefore consider their professional responsibilities and availability before applying. Government officials who normally have significant work responsibilities should pay particular attention to the employer-support requirement. Written confirmation that the applicant will not be expected to perform their regular duties during the programme is an important part of meeting the stated eligibility conditions. Applicants should also make sure they have a reliable computer and sufficient internet access to participate effectively in online sessions. Visit HERE to learn more about the UNU-MERIT MMPAF Programme 2026. Programme Funding and Partnership The MMPAF programme is funded by the European Union through the Migration Partnership Facility (MPF) of the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD) . The programme is implemented through UNU-MERIT and is aimed at strengthening capacity among civil servants and policy practitioners working in migration management across the specified regions. This international partnership reflects the broader importance of strengthening migration governance and developing the knowledge and skills of officials and practitioners responsible for migration-related policies. Frequently Asked Questions What is the MMPAF Programme? The Moving the Migration Policy Agenda Forward (MMPAF) is an online capacity-building programme focused on migration and asylum policy. It is offered by UNU-MERIT and is primarily intended for government officials working in migration and/or asylum, while also being open to other practitioners and students interested in the field. Is the MMPAF Programme online? Yes. The 2026 MMPAF courses are delivered online. How many courses are offered in 2026? Two courses are offered: Irregular Migration Migration and Development How long does each course last? Each course lasts one full-time week. How much time must participants commit? Participants are required to commit approximately 40 hours per week , including online contact hours, self-preparation and practical activities. Do I need a Bachelor s degree? Yes. The stated eligibility requirements require applicants to hold at least a Bachelor s degree. Do I need to speak English? Yes. Applicants must be fluent in both spoken and written English. Can applicants from Kenya apply? Yes. Kenya is listed among the eligible Sub-Saharan African countries. When is the application deadline? The application deadline is 4 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST . When will applicants be notified? Selection notifications are expected in mid-October 2026 . What courses are available? The 2026 programme offers Irregular Migration , running from 23–27 November 2026, and Migration and Development , running from 30 November–4 December 2026. Do government officials need employer approval? Yes. Eligible government officials are required to have full and written support from their employers confirming that they will not be expected to perform their normal work duties during the MMPAF programme. Conclusion The UNU-MERIT Moving the Migration Policy Agenda Forward (MMPAF) Programme 2026 provides a specialised online capacity-building opportunity for government officials and other professionals interested in migration and asylum policy. Through its two courses on Irregular Migration and Migration and Development , the programme combines academic instruction with interactive sessions, practical exercises, workshops and Problem-Based Learning. The programme is particularly relevant to civil servants and migration policy practitioners in eligible countries across Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Central Asia, the Silk Route and the EU Southern Neighbourhood. With Kenya and numerous other African countries included among the eligible locations , professionals in these regions can consider the programme as an opportunity to strengthen their migration-policy knowledge and practical capabilities. Prospective applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements, secure any necessary employer support and prepare their supporting documents well in advance. Since the programme requires a full-time commitment of approximately 40 hours per week, applicants should also ensure they can dedicate the necessary time to the course. The application deadline is 4 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST , with selection notifications expected in mid-October. Interested applicants should therefore complete and submit their applications before the deadline through the official UNU-MERIT application portal.
