title: Remote Research Internship at United Nations University (UNU) in Neuroscience, Learning and AI in Higher Education
summary: The United Nations University (UNU) is inviting applications for a Remote Research Intern – Neuroscience, Learning and AI in Higher Education position at the UNU Institute in Macau (UNU Macau) . This two-month research internship provides an opportunity for qualified postgraduate researchers to gain practical experience in policy-oriented research while contributing to work examining the intersection of neuroscience, learning sciences, artificial intelligence and higher education. The internship is particularly relevant for candidates with an academic background in neuroscience, education, learning sciences, psychology, artificial intelligence, social sciences or a related discipline who are interested in understanding how emerging technologies and evidence from learning and neuroscience can influence education policy and practice. The successful intern will work remotely under the supervision of the Institute Director and contribute to research for a forthcoming Springer publication on AI and higher education, alongside research briefs, policy recommendations, blogs, academic papers and other knowledge products. Financial Support The advertised position lists a payment of $550 per month . Duration The internship will last for 2 months . The anticipated internship period is: Start date: October 5, 2026 End date: December 4, 2026 Application Deadline September 18, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Macau time (GMT+8). Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline because the application page will no longer be operational after the closing date. About the United Nations University The United Nations University is an international community of scholars working on policy-oriented research, capacity development and knowledge dissemination in support of the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter. For more than four decades, UNU has served as a global research and think-tank institution working on major challenges affecting human survival, conflict prevention, sustainable development and human welfare. Its research contributes to the broader work of the United Nations and its Member States and covers issues connected to the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) . UNU brings together researchers working across different countries and disciplines. The university also maintains collaborations with United Nations agencies, universities and research institutions around the world. This makes a UNU internship particularly valuable for individuals seeking exposure to international research, evidence-based policymaking, sustainable development and the United Nations system . About UNU Institute in Macau The United Nations University Institute in Macau is one of the research and training institutes within the UNU system. UNU Macau focuses on the relationship between digital technologies and sustainable development , undertaking research designed to address challenges identified within the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The Institute emphasizes: Digital technology and sustainable development Evidence-based policymaking Data-driven approaches Applied research Innovation and emerging technologies ICT for development Interdisciplinary research Policy impact at international, regional and national levels One of the Institute s objectives is to help nurture the next generation of interdisciplinary researchers, including computing, information and social scientists and engineers working in ICT for development. The Institute s location in Macau also places it within the broader Greater Bay Area, a major technology and innovation hub with connections to China, Hong Kong SAR and several other Asian countries. For the selected intern, this provides an opportunity to participate in research connected to major technological and educational developments while working within a United Nations research environment. About the Research Internship The Research Intern – Neuroscience, Learning and AI in Higher Education will support ongoing research under the supervision of the Institute Director. The internship is connected to a forthcoming Springer publication on artificial intelligence and higher education , meaning the successful candidate will have an opportunity to contribute to research that may ultimately inform an academic publication. The role combines several areas of expertise, including: Neuroscience Learning science Education Artificial intelligence Higher education Social science research Education policy Academic writing Knowledge translation Evidence-based policymaking The position is therefore well suited to candidates who enjoy interdisciplinary research and are interested in translating academic evidence into practical policy and educational recommendations. Key Responsibilities The selected Research Intern will undertake a range of research and knowledge-production activities. 1. Conduct Literature Reviews A major responsibility will involve conducting literature reviews and research relating to: Neuroscience Learning Education Artificial intelligence Higher education The intern will be expected to identify relevant academic literature, examine existing evidence, synthesize findings and help establish an evidence base for ongoing UNU research. Strong literature-review skills will therefore be important because the role requires the ability to navigate academic research and identify information relevant to specific research questions. 2. Support Research for the Springer Book The intern will support research and analysis contributing to a forthcoming Springer book focused on AI and higher education . This could involve reviewing academic literature, organizing research materials, synthesizing findings and supporting the development of content for the publication. The opportunity may therefore be particularly attractive to candidates who want experience contributing to an international academic publication. 3. Explore Neuroscience and Learning Science The intern will examine how findings and insights from neuroscience and learning science can contribute to better educational policies and practices. This involves exploring the relationship between how people learn, what research says about learning and cognition, and how these insights can be incorporated into education systems. The role therefore goes beyond simply studying artificial intelligence. It requires an interdisciplinary understanding of how AI, learning, neuroscience and education intersect. 4. Contribute to Education Policy Recommendations Another important responsibility will be contributing to policy outputs and recommendations. The intern will explore how evidence from neuroscience and learning science can potentially inform policymaking within education. This may include helping translate academic findings into practical recommendations that policymakers and other stakeholders can understand and potentially apply. 5. Write Blogs and Research Publications The selected candidate will also contribute to various written knowledge products. These may include: Blog articles Research papers Journal articles Policy outputs Other knowledge products This means candidates should be comfortable communicating complex academic information clearly and accurately. Strong academic and analytical writing will be particularly important for this aspect of the internship. 6. Prepare and Analyze Research Materials The intern will assist with the preparation, organization and analysis of research materials and evidence. This responsibility requires attention to detail and the ability to work systematically with academic information. Expected Outputs During the internship, the successful candidate is expected to contribute to several research and knowledge products. These include: Research Briefs and Literature Reviews The intern may contribute to research briefs and comprehensive literature reviews examining neuroscience, learning, AI and higher education. Policy Recommendations The intern will contribute to recommendations examining how neuroscience and learning science can be incorporated into educational policymaking. Blog Articles and Public-Facing Content The internship also provides an opportunity to contribute to blogs and other materials designed to communicate research findings to broader audiences. Academic Publications The intern may contribute to drafts or research supporting journal articles and other academic publications. Springer Book Research A significant component of the internship will involve research and analysis contributing to the forthcoming Springer book on artificial intelligence and higher education. Learning Opportunities and Professional Development The internship is designed not only to support UNU s research activities but also to provide professional development for the selected intern. 1. Strengthen Research Skills Interns will gain practical experience conducting research in a professional international research environment. This can strengthen abilities in: Literature reviews Evidence synthesis Research analysis Academic writing Research organization Knowledge production 2. Learn to Translate Research Into Policy One of the most valuable learning objectives is developing the ability to transform research findings into policy-relevant outputs . This is particularly useful for individuals interested in careers involving: Public policy International development Education policy Research Think tanks Academia International organizations Technology policy 3. Gain United Nations Experience The internship provides exposure to the working environment of the United Nations University. Experience within a UN institution can help candidates better understand how international organizations conduct research, generate evidence and contribute to global policy discussions. 4. Work in a Multicultural Environment UNU operates within an international and multicultural environment. The internship therefore offers an opportunity to develop experience collaborating across different cultural, academic and professional backgrounds. Required Qualifications Applicants must meet the academic and professional requirements outlined for the position. Educational Requirements Candidates must have a Master s degree or higher in one of the following areas: Neuroscience Education Learning sciences Psychology Artificial intelligence Social sciences A related field The interdisciplinary nature of the position means that candidates from different academic backgrounds may be considered, provided their expertise is relevant to the research focus. Required Skills and Experience Applicants should demonstrate strong capabilities in research and academic writing. Key requirements include: Strong Research Skills Candidates should have experience conducting structured and rigorous research. Analytical Skills The position requires the ability to analyze academic evidence, identify important findings and synthesize information. Academic Writing Applicants should be capable of producing clear, well-structured academic and research-oriented writing. Literature Review Experience Candidates should demonstrate the ability to conduct literature reviews and synthesize findings from academic research. Interest in Interdisciplinary Research Applicants should have a strong interest in the intersection of: Neuroscience + Learning + Artificial Intelligence + Higher Education Ability to Work Independently Because the position is remote, applicants must be able to organize their workload, manage deadlines and work effectively with limited direct supervision. Language Requirements Candidates must have: Excellent written English Excellent spoken English Knowledge of another United Nations official language is considered an advantage. Applicants who can demonstrate multilingual communication skills may therefore have an additional strength, although English proficiency is the primary language requirement specified for the position. Core Values and Competencies The internship follows UNU s core values and competency framework. Core Values Candidates are expected to demonstrate: Respect for diversity Integrity Professionalism Core Competencies The position also emphasizes: Awareness and sensitivity regarding gender issues Accountability Creative problem solving Effective communication Inclusive collaboration Applicants should consider demonstrating these competencies through their cover letter, CV and examples of previous research or professional work. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is open to qualified candidates who meet the stated academic and skills requirements. The organization also strongly encourages applications from developing countries and women . Therefore, the announcement does not restrict applicants to a particular continent or nationality. Qualified candidates from around the world can apply, subject to meeting the academic, skills and other requirements. Application Requirements Interested applicants must submit an application containing the following materials: 1. Cover Letter Applicants should submit a brief cover letter written in English. The cover letter should explain: Why the applicant is interested in the internship Their relevant qualifications Their suitability for the research position Their interest in neuroscience, learning, AI and higher education The cover letter should be specifically tailored to the position rather than being a generic application letter. 2. Current CV Applicants must submit a current and complete CV in English . The CV should clearly demonstrate relevant: Academic qualifications Research experience Publications or academic writing Professional experience Analytical skills Relevant projects Research interests 3. Examples of Relevant Research Work Applicants must provide examples of relevant research work in English. This could be particularly important because the internship is heavily research-focused. This requirement should be taken seriously when preparing for the internship because the selected intern is responsible for having the required insurance coverage. The assessment process may include: Desk review of applications Competency-based interview Reference checks Candidates should therefore prepare to discuss their academic background, research experience, analytical abilities, writing skills and motivation for joining UNU. A competency-based interview may also explore examples of how candidates have demonstrated communication, accountability, problem solving, collaboration and other relevant competencies. Important Information About the Remote Internship The position is explicitly described as a remote internship . This means applicants do not need to relocate to Macau to carry out the internship. However, candidates should understand that remote work still requires: Reliable communication Independent time management Consistent availability Ability to meet deadlines Strong written communication Ability to collaborate virtually Access to an appropriate working environment Visa and Employment Considerations UNU states that it does not sponsor a working visa for this position. Because this is a remote internship, applicants should carefully consider the location from which they will undertake the internship and ensure they can legally participate from that location. Therefore, candidates should not regard the internship as a guaranteed pathway to a permanent or temporary position within the organization. Applicants should therefore distinguish between gaining experience through a UNU internship and being employed as a member of the United Nations international civil service. Why This Internship Could Be Valuable for Researchers This opportunity offers several potential benefits for postgraduate researchers and early-career professionals. Interdisciplinary Experience The internship brings together several rapidly developing fields, including artificial intelligence, neuroscience, learning sciences and higher education. title: C. B. Facey Foundation Grants 2026: Funding Opportunities for Arts, Education and Environmental Initiatives in Jamaica
summary: The C. B. Facey Foundation provides funding and support for initiatives that contribute to the development of communities through its mandated areas of Arts, Education and the Environment . The Foundation accepts grant applications during a specific annual application period, while sponsorship and ticket purchase requests can be submitted throughout the year for consideration. For organizations, community groups, institutions and other eligible applicants working within the Foundation s areas of interest, this presents an opportunity to seek financial support for initiatives that align with the Foundation s mandate. About the C. B. Facey Foundation The C. B. Facey Foundation supports activities and initiatives within three principal areas: Arts Education Environment Its support is structured through different avenues, including annual grant applications, sponsorship requests and specific scholarship arrangements. Applicants should understand that these avenues have different application procedures and timelines. In particular, the annual grant application period should not be confused with sponsorship requests, which can be submitted year-round. C. B. Facey Foundation Grant Applications The Foundation accepts grant applications annually from August 12 to October 12 . This annual application window provides an opportunity for applicants seeking financial support for eligible initiatives to submit their proposals for consideration. Application period The annual grant application period is: Opening date: August 12 Deadline: October 12 each year APPLY HERE Applicants interested in receiving grant support should therefore prepare their proposals and supporting information before the application period opens. Because applications are only accepted during the specified annual period, applicants should pay close attention to the dates and ensure that their submissions are made within the Foundation s designated window. Areas Covered by the Foundation The Foundation s mandate covers three major areas: Arts, Education and the Environment. 1. Arts Organizations and initiatives working within the arts may fall within one of the Foundation s areas of interest. This may include activities connected to artistic and cultural development, although the information provided does not specify a complete list of eligible arts projects or the maximum amount that can be requested. Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed initiative clearly demonstrates its relevance to the Foundation s arts mandate. 2. Education Education is another core area supported by the C. B. Facey Foundation. Applicants seeking support for education-related initiatives should ensure that their proposals demonstrate a clear connection to educational development and fall within the Foundation s mandated areas. The Foundation also provides scholarships through specific educational institutions, but these scholarships operate separately from the general grant application process. 3. Environment Environmental initiatives are also included within the Foundation s mandate. However, applicants should distinguish between the Foundation s general grant applications and the Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant , which is specifically intended for conservation projects. Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant The Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant Application is designed for conservation projects. According to the information provided, the Eco-Grant application is currently closed . This means applicants interested specifically in conservation funding should not assume that the general C. B. Facey Foundation grant application period automatically applies to the Eco-Grant. Those interested in future conservation funding opportunities should monitor the relevant application announcements for information about when the Eco-Grant reopens. Sponsorship Opportunities The C. B. Facey Foundation also considers sponsorship and ticket purchase requests separately from its annual grant applications. Unlike the annual grants, sponsorship and ticket purchase requests can be submitted year-round . Requests must fall within the Foundation s mandated areas of: Arts Education Environment Applicants or organizations seeking sponsorship should submit their requests by email to: cbfacey@panjamaica.com This means organizations do not necessarily have to wait until the August 12 to October 12 grant application period to request sponsorship or ticket purchase support. However, submitting a request does not guarantee funding or sponsorship. Requests are subject to consideration by the Foundation. How Sponsorship Requests Work Those seeking sponsorship or requesting ticket purchases should prepare their request clearly and explain the purpose of the support being sought. A strong request should make it easy for the Foundation to understand: Who is making the request. What activity, event or initiative is being proposed. Whether the request relates to Arts, Education or the Environment. What type of sponsorship or ticket purchase support is being requested. Why the initiative is relevant to the Foundation s mandate. The Foundation can then consider the request based on its own criteria and priorities. Scholarship Opportunities The C. B. Facey Foundation also provides scholarships, but these scholarships are not open through a general Foundation application process . The Foundation specifically states that it grants scholarships only to: Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture This is an important distinction for prospective applicants. Students interested in these scholarships must apply through the bursaries of the respective institutions . Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts Students interested in scholarships associated with the Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts should contact and apply through the institution s bursary. Applicants should not send a separate scholarship application directly to the C. B. Facey Foundation unless specifically instructed to do so. UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture Students interested in scholarships associated with the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture must similarly apply through the institution s bursary. The Foundation s information does not indicate that these scholarships are available to students at other universities or colleges. Important Difference Between Grants, Sponsorships and Scholarships Applicants should understand the differences between the Foundation s support mechanisms. Support Type Application Period Main Areas/Recipients General Grants August 12 – October 12 annually Arts, Education and Environment Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant Currently closed Conservation projects Sponsorships/Ticket Purchases Year-round Arts, Education and Environment Scholarships Through respective institutions Edna Manley College and UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture This distinction is important because each opportunity follows a different process. For example, someone seeking funding for an eligible organizational project may need to use the annual grant application process, while someone seeking event sponsorship can submit a request by email throughout the year. Similarly, a student seeking one of the Foundation s scholarships should approach the relevant institution s bursary rather than submitting a general scholarship application to the Foundation. Deadline for C. B. Facey Foundation Grant Applications The annual grant application deadline is: October 12 each year The application period begins on August 12 . Applicants should therefore make sure that their applications are submitted before October 12 rather than waiting until the final day. For sponsorship and ticket purchase requests, there is no annual deadline , as requests can be emailed year-round. The Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant is currently closed. How to Contact the C. B. Facey Foundation Applicants and interested individuals who have questions or concerns can contact the Foundation directly. Email: cbfacey@panjamaica.com Telephone: 876-929-4510 The email address can be used for questions relating to grants, sponsorships, ticket purchase requests and other matters within the Foundation s mandate. Visit HERE to learn more about the C. B. Facey Foundation Grants 2026 Who Should Consider Applying? Potential applicants include those involved in: Arts and cultural initiatives Educational initiatives Environmental initiatives Conservation-related projects, when the relevant Eco-Grant is open Events or activities seeking sponsorship within the Foundation s mandated areas Students should note that the scholarship component is much more specific. According to the information provided, scholarships are limited to students applying through the bursaries of Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts and the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture . What Applicants Should Keep in Mind Before submitting a request, applicants should first determine which type of support best matches their needs. If you are seeking grant funding , check whether your initiative fits within Arts, Education or the Environment and prepare your application for the August 12–October 12 annual window. If you are seeking sponsorship or ticket purchases , you can submit your request by email at any time during the year. If you are seeking a scholarship , confirm whether you are applying through one of the two institutions identified by the Foundation and submit your application through the appropriate bursary. If your project is specifically focused on conservation , be aware that the Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant is currently closed and that a separate announcement may be required when applications reopen. Conclusion The C. B. Facey Foundation offers several forms of support for initiatives connected to Arts, Education and the Environment . Its main grant application period runs annually from August 12 to October 12 , giving eligible applicants a defined window in which to seek grant funding. Beyond the annual grant programme, the Foundation accepts sponsorship and ticket purchase requests throughout the year by email. Meanwhile, its scholarship support is specifically directed to students at Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts and the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture , with applications handled through the respective institutions bursaries. Applicants should carefully identify the appropriate funding route before submitting a request and ensure that their initiative falls within the Foundation s stated areas of support.
